Blog
Declarative Schemas for Simpler Database Management
03 Apr 2025
•
7 minute read
Qiao Han
Engineering
Today we’re releasing declarative schemas to simplify managing and maintaining complex database schemas. With declarative schemas, you can define your database structure in a clear, centralized, and version-controlled manner.
What are declarative schemas?
#
Declarative schemas store the final desired state of the database in
.sql
files that can be saved and versioned alongside a project. For example, here is the declarative schema for a classic
products
table:
_
10
create table "products" (
_
10
"id" serial primary key,
_
10
"name" text not null,
_
10
"description" text,
_
10
"price" numeric(10,2) not null,
_
10
"created_at" timestamp default now()
_
10
);
_
10
_
10
alter table "products"
_
10
enable row level security;
Declarative schemas offer numerous benefits over making changes to your database schema directly:
Single pane of glass
. Maintain your entire database schema in one place, reducing redundancy and potential errors.
Versioned migrations
. Automatically generate migration files, ensuring consistent schema updated across environments. Store your declarative schema files alongside your project files in your version control system.
Concise code reviews
. Easily review changes to tables, views, and functions without manually repeating complex migration scripts.
Declarative schemas vs migrations
#
It's best practice to use
Migrations
to track and apply changes to databases. Every time you make a change, you create a new new file with all the changes, keeping changes versioned and reproducible.
However, as the complexity of a database schemas grows, it becomes increasingly difficult to develop using versioned migrations as there isn't a single place to see the entire database schema.
For example, at Supabase we have a complex and frequently-updated
projects
table. Here's partially what it looks like with RLS enabled:
_
32
create table private.projects (
_
32
id              bigint    not null,
_
32
name            text      not null,
_
32
organization_id bigint    not null,
_
32
inserted_at     timestamp not null,
_
32
updated_at      timestamp not null
_
32
);
_
32
_
32
alter table private.projects
_
32
enable row level security;
_
32
_
32
create policy projects_insert
_
32
on private.projects
_
32
for insert
_
32
to authenticated
_
32
with check auth.can_write(project_id);
_
32
_
32
create policy projects_select
_
32
on private.projects
_
32
for select
_
32
to authenticated
_
32
using auth.can_read(project_id);
_
32
_
32
-- Users can only view the projects that they have access to
_
32
create view public.projects as select
_
32
projects.id,
_
32
projects.name,
_
32
projects.organization_id,
_
32
projects.inserted_at,
_
32
projects.updated_at
_
32
from private.projects
_
32
where auth.can_read(projects.id);
The
projects
table is created in a private schema, with a public view exposed for reads. Attribute-based access control (ABAC) is implemented on top of RLS policies to ensure queries only return projects that the user has access to.
Since Postgres views are not updatable by default, we have defined trigger functions to cascade writes to the underlying table when a Supabase user creates a new project. This makes development easier because the
projects
view can be inserted with regular PostgREST calls while invoking the appropriate RLS policies on the underlying table.
_
24
-- Triggers to update views from PostgREST: select('projects').insert({ ... })
_
24
create function public.public_projects_on_insert() returns trigger
_
24
as $$
_
24
begin
_
24
insert into private.projects(
_
24
name,
_
24
organization_id,
_
24
inserted_at,
_
24
updated_at
_
24
) values (
_
24
NEW.name,
_
24
NEW.organization_id,
_
24
coalesce(NEW.inserted_at, now()),
_
24
coalesce(NEW.updated_at, now())
_
24
) returning * into NEW;
_
24
return NEW;
_
24
end
_
24
$$ language plpgsql;
_
24
_
24
create trigger public_projects_on_insert
_
24
instead of insert
_
24
on public.projects
_
24
for each row
_
24
execute function public.public_projects_on_insert();
This complexity slows down development velocity, as changes to the table might break other views or functions. Back in early 2022, a simple change to add a new column involved the following steps.
Find the latest schema for
projects
table in our migration files or by querying our database.
Write the
alter table
statement in a new migration file.
Copy and update the
projects
view definition to include the new column.
Copy and update the trigger function definition to include the new column.
Add new pgTAP tests and verify that existing tests pass.
Submit the new migration file for review, which would be at least a few hundred lines.
This process is tedious and it's frustrating to have multiple engineers working on the
projects
table concurrently. Merging PRs would result in a merge conflict that must be resolved by repeating steps 1-5.
Using declarative schemas in product

• bartvk 总结了新旧方法的对比，旧方法需要手动编写 ALTER TABLE 脚本，而新方法只需修改 CREATE TABLE 脚本，工具自动计算差异并执行变更。这种方法消除了新建和更新数据库之间的差异。
• joshAg 表示自动生成迁移脚本可能导致问题，特别是在处理枚举变更、非空列添加和数据迁移时，这些操作在迁移脚本中更容易实现。
• neutralino1 提到 Rails 多年来的做法类似且更好，通过保持原子性和历史迁移，同时维护一个 schema.sql 文件用于测试等场景。
• Guillaume86 希望将这种方法移到一个独立的 CLI 工具中，并提到微软的 SSDT 方案，强调声明式 schema 管理的好处，如错误检查、引用查找等。
• oulipo 提到使用 Drizzle 等工具定义表和处理迁移的相似性。
• ucarion 关心生成的迁移脚本是否可以手动编辑，比如添加并发索引。
• kiwicopple 提到结合 Postgres 语言服务器，可以在 IDE 中直接执行语句。
• geocar 警告自动生成迁移可能带来的风险，特别是在 CI 中自动加载迁移可能导致未来问题，且修复成本高昂。
• xaas 提到使用 ZenStack，并指出其未来版本将脱离 supabase。
• mylons 质疑这种方法相比原始 SQL 的优势。
• wmanley 提供了一些相关的参考文章，并披露自己是其中一篇的合著者。

补充讨论：
- 声明式与命令式方法的优劣对比是核心争议点。
- 自动生成迁移脚本的可靠性和可控性受到质疑，特别是在处理复杂数据库变更时。
- 不同工具和框架（如 Rails、SSDT、ZenStack）的实现和优劣被提及。
- 手动编辑和检查迁移脚本的重要性被多次强调。

I Want a Better Mac, so Iâm Cheering for a Better Linux
By
Timothy R. Butler
| Posted at
11:04 PM
My
recent column
on Appleâs declining software quality hit a nerve. So why do any of us put up with software that grows increasingly buggy? One word: hardware.
Telling in many of the comments about my piece was a repeated refrain, âAppleâs software keeps getting worse, but I canât imagine going through the downgrade to other hardware.â Apple knows how to turn out very good quality pieces of hardware and, for many purposes, stands alone.
Thatâs been largely true for the last couple of decades. The half-decade of Apple Silicon has cemented this position. At any price point Apple contends, Macs, iPads and iPhones are either without peers or at the top of the market in build quality and processing power. The Mac mini isnât the cheapest computer, nor is the base iPad the cheapest tablet, but they are the cheapest
good
options and so it goes on up.
Appleâs hardware is not just good; it is designed carefully to work together. While making the case about software bugs, I alluded to various functions that make abandoning ship more than just a downgrade in pure hardware quality. Even with a âgood enoughâ tablet, acceptable earbuds and a decent phone, nothing works together at the same level Apple has achieved.
Do I want to give up using my tablet as an instantaneously available wireless display that automatically shares my laptopâs keyboard and touchpad? Do I want to give up having earbuds that flow between devices without so much as a button press?
Even buggy software gains a sheen in an environment of close integration of excellent devices. Had Steve Jobs embraced Mac clones in the late 1990s, an idea that would have made Apple primarily a software company, the flaws in MacOS and iOS — if they even still existed — would be only more glaring.
Uniquely well crafted and integrated hardware covers a multitude of software sins. We always use hardware and software together, so the sum of the parts is what matters. Even with diminishing quality, MacOS and iOS hold this card over the Windows-Android alternative, hamstrung as it is by a vast array of manufacturersâ varied, often contradictory, and routinely inferior hardware design choices.
Numerous responses to my piece on software hit a similar impulse to my own: if only there were hardware that was as good and worked together as well as Appleâs, jumping ship to Linux would be awfully attractive at this juncture. The mainstream Linux desktop, an ever elusive goal
this publication was founded to advocate for a quarter century ago
, feels so incredibly, tantalizingly close today.
For Apple aficionados troubled by the state of MacOS, the modern GNOME desktop on Linux beckons as a more faithful implementation of the ideals of MacOS than current MacOS does. GNOME is painstakingly consistent across its different apps and exudes the minimalist philosophy with which Appleâs hardware shines. Gone are the rough edges that always hindered the Linux desktop when I used to write about it regularly.
I helped a number of friends and colleagues make the jump to Linux desktops against the currents in the early 2000s when it was still weird. But, none of those Linux âmigrationâ projects, even my own, stuck over the long haul. The intersection where software meets hardware was always the problem. Some part of the computer wouldnât fully work under Linux or some necessary peripheral couldnât talk to it. That was bad in a largely desktop era; itâs a non-starter in the laptop, tablet and phone era.
My first attempt at a non-Windows laptop was a Dell Pentium III laptop retrofit with a then-current variant of Linux. It worked ok, but not great. One upside: anything worked better than the Windows ME it came with. (Credit: Timothy R. Butler)
And this was before something like a tablet seamlessly sharing a mouse and keyboard with a computer was even a dream.
Recent editions of MacOS and iOS may not work as well as we users would like, but thereâs no current combination of computers and accessories that can achieve a complete replacement. Apple reigns here, while Windows at least benefits from broad manufacturer support. Linux still suffers from largely being a platform added onto hardware and made to work with accessories intended for something else.
The Windows-Android complex is largely content with middling software on subpar hardware. Apple offers something better in terms of hardware, but it isnât âhungryâ enough in the post-Jobs era. Tim Cookâs iteration of the company is content to coast with the minimally acceptable software quality it can pass off to sell that hardware.
So long as no one is competing on making better quality software, the present software quality morass will continue.

data.title: Digital Archivists: Protecting Public Data from Erasure
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了哈佛大学法学院的图书馆创新实验室如何利用API技术保存公共信息，避免其消失在"记忆黑洞"中。该项目专注于创建Data.gov网站的存档，该网站包含31.1万个公共数据集。通过这种方法，数字档案管理员确保了重要公共数据的长久保存和可访问性，为未来的研究和分析提供了宝贵的资源。文章强调了技术在保护和维护公共信息方面的重要性，展示了创新技术如何应用于信息保存领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：数据存档、公开记录以及隐私问题

不同观点：
• dmillar：许多犯罪记录，无论是轻微还是严重的，都是公开记录。即使是被删除或撤销的违规记录，仍可能在背景调查中出现，因为公司会存档公共数据。因此，即使是撤销的记录也有可能被公开。

• badlibrarian：在数据存档领域存在很多恐慌和重叠工作，需要一种协调这些努力的方法。Internet Archive等组织虽然引起了关注并做出了承诺，但最终因无法处理大量数据而让志愿者停止存档工作。同时，也提到了其他团队的努力，如Archive Team和Webrecorder。

• nla：引用BBC档案负责人的观点，强调一旦进行了格式转换，就需要一直进行格式转换。因此，建议尽可能保留原始资料。

• Damogran6：假设政府领导人宣布删除数据，引发 rush 去备份数据，随后政府领导人宣称他们将维护数据的成本转移出了政府，从而实现了更小、更高效的政府。对此表示反感。

• mikrl：讨论了与dox相关的问题，如果个人在公共场所发布了身份识别或 incriminating 信息，第三方存储并可能让他人访问这些信息。如果原始发布者删除了信息但无法彻底清除，这些信息是否仍被视为公开的？它是否曾经真正公开过？

补充讨论：
• Teever：提到之前提交的相关内容被标记，强调讨论这些内容的重要性，希望当前提交的内容不会被标记。

• hsuduebc2：提出区块链技术是否可以在数据存档和隐私问题上提供有效解决方案的疑问。

争议焦点：
• 数据一旦公开或存档后，是否能够以及如何彻底删除或保护隐私。特别是在第三方存档和区块链技术的应用上存在不同看法。

data.title: Bikes in the Age of Tariffs
data.author: bobchadwick
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了关税对自行车行业的影响，特别是对Rene Herse Cycles等公司的冲击。美国对进口产品加征高额关税，旨在促进国内生产，但同时导致进口商品价格上涨。虽然自行车行业长期以来已有不同类别的关税，但新关税按原产国设定，尤其是针对中国，目前中国制造的自行车关税已高达69%。这对高端自行车影响较小，因为其生产已转移出中国，但碳纤维车架和组件可能因模具专用性仍部分依赖中国生产。总体而言，关税将导致自行车价格上升，并对行业造成深远影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关税政策的影响及相关政治动机

不同观点：
• [mullingitover] 认为，面对加税，最大限度地投入资金以惩罚相关方是财务上负责任的做法。这暗示了通过政治捐赠来对抗税收政策的立场。
• [whynotmaybe] 通过具体计算展示了关税对商品价格的直接影响，例如儿童自行车成本的增加。这说明了关税如何导致商品价格上涨。
• [rstarast] 提出，不同国家之间的关税差异可能会导致进口商品的重新routing和重新label。他们质疑现有控制措施的有效性。
• [crawdog] 指出，关税对美国制造商的供应链影响被忽视了，特别是在汽车制造商的长期合同中。他们认为这会导致价格上涨，并质疑政策的长期效果。
• [osigurdson] 补充说明，高档山地自行车的碳纤维车架主要在台湾制造，而非中国，这涉及到关税对不同生产地的影响。
• [giraffe_lady] 引用了关于国际贸易如何使小众产品实现规模经济的见解，认为这是一个常被忽视的因素。
• [mmooss] 提出了对关税政策的潜在政治动机的质疑，认为右翼可能通过制造经济危机来传播恐惧和仇恨，以达到政治目的。
• [metalman] 认为大型制造商的巨额利润使得“财务不可行”的说法不成立，并提出小型制造商的兴起可能对全球社区有益。但也承认存在事情向更糟方向发展的风险。

• [typeofhuman] 批评文章以美国为中心的观点，指出其他国家长期以来也在实施关税政策。

Bikes in the Age of Tariffs
Jan Heine
2025-04-03T10:22:33-07:00
Today’s post was going to be about a new product we’re introducing—but we need to hold off while we recalculate our prices. You’ve probably seen the news: Virtually all imports into the United States will be subjected to additional, steep import taxes, also called tariffs. The goal is to radically re-orient how manufacturing is done, and to make things domestically. Tariffs tend to be reciprocal, so most countries will increase their tariffs on American-made goods, too.
Our rulers seem to think that the U.S. imports more than it exports, so the net effect will be positive. Whether that is true is open to debate. Look at the graphic above, published in the
Wall Street Journal
. What strikes me is how large the volume of imports and exports really is. Sure, there is a trade deficit, but the size of the exports (the green part) is far greater than the deficit. And all that will also be affected by the new tariffs in one way or another.
The bike industry isn’t even an afterthought in these decisions, and yet it’ll be affected deeply by all of them. Let’s look at how the tariffs will reshape our industry and our sport.
What are tariffs?
Tariffs are a tax on imported goods. They are assessed when those goods enter the country, and the importer pays them. Usually, they are added to the freight costs. Shipments are released by customs only after any applicable tariffs (and associated fees) are paid.
Some have suggested that foreign suppliers will pay at least for part of the tariffs by reducing their prices to remain competitive in the U.S. In our experience, that is unlikely. At least in the bike industry, most suppliers are unaware of the tariffs that their good face after leaving the country. They never see them. They calculate their prices based on their cost structure. Even retail giants like Walmart reportedly have been rebuffed when asking suppliers for price breaks to account for part of the tariffs. The simple reality is that in a free market system, only suppliers with lean cost structures survive. There isn’t room for cutting prices by 10, 20, 30% or more.
In summary, tariffs are an added tax on imported goods. Like all sales taxes, it’s regressive, because those with less income spend a larger percentage of their money on buying things.
Existing tariffs
There have been tariffs on bicycles all along. They varied by category, since they were intended to protect domestic producers. Complete bicycles were assessed an 11% tax upon import, but lightweight adult bikes saw only 5.5%. This made sense. Way back, companies like Huffy and Schwinn made the vast majority of kid’s and adult bikes domestically, but high-end bikes were usually imported. The same applied to parts: 11% was the base rate, but parts like freewheel hubs and cotterless aluminum cranks did not have any import duty. Nor did bicycle tires. Because nobody was making these parts in the U.S.
The general idea was to protect certain domestic industries against imports, no matter where they came from. And for things that nobody in the U.S. was making, the idea was to facilitate importing them. As an example, Schwinn made almost everything they needed to build bicycles in their huge Chicago factory (above)—but even they imported derailleurs and other parts for high-end bikes.
A new way to do tariffs
The new tariffs are different: The rates are set not by product category, but by country of origin. Instead of protecting specific domestic industries, the goal appears to be punishing certain countries—and, by extension, American companies that source their products from these countries.
This article is about the impact on the bike industry. How will these country-by-country rates affect the bike world and Rene Herse Cycles in particular?
China — 69%
Tariffs on China have been in the headlines for years. For made-in-China bicycles, a 10% tariff has been in place since the mid-2010s, plus another 25% tariff was enacted in 2018. Yesterday, a 34% tariff was added. If my math is correct, that would put the tariff at a whopping 69%.
However, the impact of the new tariffs on performance bikes will be small. The earlier tariffs added 35% to the price of Chinese bikes and frames. They had the effect of moving most bicycle production out of China, at least for high-end products where manufacturing (and not shipping, warehousing and marketing) makes up most of the costs. One possible exception is the manufacture of carbon frames and components (especially rims), where some companies have significant investments in molds at Chinese factories. Generally, tooling is specific to the machines and techniques of one supplier and cannot be moved from factory to factory, much less from country to country.

data.title: Rewriting my site in vanilla web
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
作者讲述了重构自己网站的经历，从使用各种库和框架，到自己创建名为 *compose-html* 的静态网站生成器，最终发现复杂度不减反增。于是，作者尝试使用纯 HTML/CSS/JS 重写网站，避免不必要的构建步骤和框架。

作者选择通过 Web Components 实现重复内容（如页眉、页脚）的模块化，利用浏览器对 HTML 标签的宽容性，省略一些常见标签。为了保持代码简洁和可维护性，作者遵循以下原则：
1. **语义化 HTML**：使用有意义的标签而非泛滥的 `div` 和 `span`。
2. **TAC CSS 方法**：使用自定义标签而非类选择器（如 BEM），简化 CSS。
3. **轻量级 Web Components**：避免 Shadow DOM 的复杂性，直接操作 Light DOM。

最终，作者认为这种方法可行，既减少了构建复杂性，又保持了灵活性，适合实际需求。

• 技术应用场景：mgr86特别指出其工作环境中存在大量XML和XSLT文件，并且这些文件用于内容供给。他认为web组件技术能够有效整合这些现有资源，从而提升工作效率和效果。

43574701.article_content:
I rewrote this website in vanilla HTML/CSS/JS. Here’s the story. But why? Over the years, I’ve used a bunch of libraries & frameworks to build this website , before finally making my own static site generator that I called compose-html . As the name suggests, it composes HTML files together, very much like Astro . compose-html’s README I like systems that have a small set of tight abstractions that are easy to understand. I’m not a fan of rigid, non-atomic concepts like “pages” and “layouts”, “themes”, “frontmatters”—I mean, these are just ‘components’ and ‘data’! I dislike those that dictate your project directory structure and coding style. If your documentation has a ‘Project structure’ section, I’m out! So I built my own simple site builder and that was nice BUT it didn’t end up making life easier. The real world is messy, and HTML more so. Simply composing pieces of HTML together isn’t that straightforward and the abstraction leaked. My compose-html framework eventually turned into a 2k LoC that was more liability than freedom. Though it served me very well, it was a dead end. Maybe nothing can solve my problem… As in, literally nothing. No framework. No build steps. What if HTML wasn’t a render target, but was both the authoring and publishing medium? What if I rewrote my site in vanilla HTML/CSS/JS? A crazy idea infiltrated my conciousness. Is it feasible? A common reason for adding complexity is to avoid repetitive work like copying headers & footers to every page. So we have PHP, Handlebars, Next.JS. Modern HTML/JS now has Web Components , custom elements which could be used to encapsulate repetitive sections! This was already possible without Web Components, but it makes it nicer. One could go write HTML like this:
My page's content

data.title: Office of the United States Trade Representative Reciprocal Tariff Calculations
data.author: shidoshi
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了通过互惠关税来平衡美国与其贸易伙伴之间的双边贸易逆差问题。由于美国长期存在贸易逆差，传统贸易模型假设的贸易自动平衡并未实现。贸易逆差由关税和非关税壁垒等多种因素导致，包括监管障碍、税收差异、货币操纵等，这些因素抑制了美国商品出口，导致贸易失衡。为解决此问题，文章提出计算能使贸易逆差归零的关税水平，即互惠关税。通过模型推导和参数选择，文章计算出互惠关税率范围在0%至99%之间，未加权平均为20%，按进口加权平均为41%。这些关税率旨在抵消导致贸易失衡的政策和经济因素，以实现公平贸易。

43574751.article_content:
Executive Summary
Reciprocal tariffs are calculated as the tariff rate necessary to balance bilateral trade deficits between the U.S. and each of our trading partners. This calculation assumes that persistent trade deficits are due to a combination of tariff and non-tariff factors that prevent trade from balancing. Tariffs work through direct reductions of imports.
Reciprocal tariff rates range from 0 percent to 99 percent, with unweighted and import-weighted averages of 20 percent and 41 percent.
Introduction
To conceptualize reciprocal tariffs, the tariff rates that would drive bilateral trade deficits to zero were computed. While models of international trade generally assume that trade will balance itself over time, the United States has run persistent current account deficits for five decades, indicating that the core premise of most trade models is incorrect.
The failure of trade deficits to balance has many causes, with tariff and non-tariff economic fundamentals as major contributors. Regulatory barriers to American products, environmental reviews, differences in consumption tax rates, compliance hurdles and costs, currency manipulation and undervaluation all serve to deter American goods and keep trade balances distorted.  As a result, U.S. consumer demand has been siphoned out of the U.S. economy into the global economy, leading to the closure of more than 90,000 American factories since 1997, and a decline in our manufacturing workforce of more than 6.6 million jobs, more than a third from its peak.
While individually computing the trade deficit effects of tens of thousands of tariff, regulatory, tax and other policies in each country is complex, if not impossible, their combined effects can be proxied by computing the tariff level consistent with driving bilateral trade deficits to zero.
If trade deficits are persistent because of tariff and non-tariff policies and fundamentals, then the tariff rate consistent with offsetting these policies and fundamentals is reciprocal and fair.
Basic Approach
Consider an environment in which the U.S. levies a tariff of rate τ_i on country i and ∆τ_i reflects the change in the tariff rate. Let ε<0 represent the elasticity of imports with respect to import prices, let φ>0 represent the passthrough from tariffs to import prices, let m_i>0 represent total imports from country i, and let x_i>0 represent total exports. Then the decrease in imports due to a change in tariffs equals ∆τ_i*ε*φ*m_i<0. Assuming that offsetting exchange rate and general equilibrium effects are small enough to be ignored, the reciprocal tariff that results in a bilateral trade balance of zero satisfies:
Parameter Selection
To calculate reciprocal tariffs, import and export data from the U.S. Census Bureau for 2024. Parameter values for ε and φ were selected. The price elasticity of import demand, ε, was set at 4.
Recent evidence suggests the elasticity is near 2 in the long run (Boehm et al., 2023), but estimates of the elasticity vary. To be conservative, studies that find higher elasticities near 3-4 (e.g., Broda and Weinstein 2006; Simonovska and Waugh 2014; Soderbery 2018) were drawn on.  The elasticity of import prices with respect to tariffs, φ, is 0.25. The recent experience with U.S. tariffs on China has demonstrated that tariff passthrough to retail prices was low (Cavallo et al, 2021).
Findings
The reciprocal tariffs were left-censored at zero. Higher minimum rates might be necessary to limit heterogeneity in rates and reduce transshipment. Tariff rates range from 0 to 99 percent. The unweighted average across deficit countries is 50 percent, and the unweighted average across the entire globe is 20 percent. Weighted by imports, the average across deficit countries is 45 percent, and the average across the entire globe is 41 percent. Standard deviations range from 20.5 to 31.8 percentage points.
References
Boehm, Christoph E., Andrei A. Levchenko, and Nitya Panalai-Nayar (2023), “The long and short of (run) of trade elasticities, American Economic Review, 113(4), 861-905.
Broda, Christian and David E. Weinstein (2006). “Globalization and the gains from variety,” Quarterly Journal of Economics, 121(2), 541-585.
Pujolas, Pau and Jack Rossbach (2024). “Trade deficits with trade wars.” SSRN.
Simonovska, Ina and Michael E. Waugh (2014). “The elasticity of trade: Estimates and evidence,” Journal of International Economics, 92(1), 34-50.
Soderberry, Anson (2018). “Trade elasticities, heterogeneity, and optimal tariffs,” Journal of International Economics, 114, 44-62.

data.title: Porting Tailscale to Plan 9
data.author: adriangrigore
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Tailscale团队在2025年4月1日愚人节宣布将Tailscale移植到Plan 9操作系统的背后故事。最初，团队认为只需简单调整构建标签和路径即可完成移植，但在实际操作中发现Go编译器对Plan 9的支持已经退化，导致运行时崩溃。经过多番努力，包括修复Go编译器中的Plan 9特殊情况以及解决SSE指令和内存管理问题，最终在2025年3月完成了实际可运行的Plan 9移植版本。团队特别感谢前Go团队成员Russ Cox的帮助，他解决了Plan 9内核中保存和恢复SSE寄存器的问题，使得移植得以成功。最终，Tailscale现在确实能够在Plan 9上运行。

work
. (Otherwise it’s 100% sad instead of whatever percent sad yesterday’s post was.)
And to be super clear today on April 2nd because nobody believes anything on April 1st: Tailscale now actually works on Plan 9. For reals.
We were amused to find everybody in shock that there was
a PR
attached to yesterday’s blog post so let’s dig into that PR a bit, and other work that went on.
First off: I don’t really know Plan 9. I know
of
Plan 9, and I know people who know Plan 9, but I’m a Plan 9 newbie and I apologize in advance if I offend any Plan 9 people with my ignorance. I tried to check my cluelessness with others to make sure it’s not
too
stupid, but there are surely some inaccuracies in these posts and bugs and shortcuts and simplifying assumptions in the code.
Anyway.
As the quip goes, “We chose to port Tailscale to Plan 9 not because it was easy, but because we thought it would be easy.” Naively it kinda seems like you’d take Tailscale’s two Go binaries and build them with
GOOS=plan9 GOARCH=386 go install ./cmd/tailscale{,d}
and call it a day. Sure, I expected some
syscall
or
x/net
or
x/sys/unix
symbols to not exists with
GOOS=plan9
and some
//go:build
tag adjustments and some special cases for
runtime.GOOS == "plan9"
to use different default disk paths like we previously
did for AIX
, etc. So that’s
what I tried
in August 2023 when a local acquaintance here in Seattle
asked me for Plan 9 support
and I finally caved and said okay (after initially rejecting the idea). I tweaked some build tags & paths & compiled it and ….
Boom
. The binary crashed at runtime in weird ways. Turns out the Go compiler support for Plan 9 had bitrot. Plan 9 wasn’t one of Go’s
first-class ports
and nobody had noticed the regressions. Or maybe Tailscale just pushed Go a bit harder than it had been pushed on Plan 9 before.
In any case, the Tailscale Plan 9 effort stalled out through all of 2024, beyond my time and/or ability to fix.
At the beginning of March 2025, a coworker mentioned April Fools’ Day and I suddenly remembered our Plan 9 port.
I reached out to
Russ Cox
(a former coworker from the Go team with a lot of Plan 9 history) and told him I thought it’d be fun (& funny) to finish up in time for April 1st. He replied:
“Sure I’m in.
We should fix the plan 9 kernel to save those registers and then not have that special case anymore.”
It’s possible that Russ didn’t know what he was signing himself up for.
SSE
In 1999, Intel introduced the Pentium III processor with
SSE instructions
. Yesterday’s blog post is dated 1999 because that’s kinda where this whole adventure begins.
The “special case” that Russ was referring to above is how the Go compiler
tried to avoid using SSE anywhere
for Plan 9 targets because the Plan 9 kernel doesn’t allow SSE in “note handlers” (think: signal handlers), as it didn’t save/restore them. And because the Go compiler didn’t know which code was being used during a note handler, it conservatively tried to disable SSE everywhere. But that code was regularly breaking and there were too many
plan9
special
cases
throughout the compiler.
Ideally the Plan 9 kernel would just save/restore the SSE registers/context in note handlers, then Go could remove the Plan 9 special cases and treat it like every other operating system. So Russ did that.
For 386, the Plan 9 fix was
sys/src/9: allow floating point in note handlers
(and updating the docs in
sys/man/2: update notify
).
For amd64 (the 9k kernel), we ran into a
bunch more issues
. Russ fixed various things:
sys/src/9k: fix bug aliasing parent and child FP state after fork
sys/src/9k: allow floating point and simd in note handlers
sys/src/9k: fix noted(NCONT) losing registers
sys/src/libmach: fix default amd64 binary mapping
sys/src/cmd/ktrace: fix for new k10 kernel trap routine
… but by this time we’d both pretty much resigned to just focusing on making the demo work on
GOARCH=386
.
With the corresponding Go fix to
stop (incorrectly) special casing Plan 9’s code generation
,
tailscaled
could now start up and run (for longer) without crashing. I could then start working on the bits that I could fix.
IPC
Now it was crashing due to out of memory errors instead of stack corruption. It turns out an earlier attempt at porting Tailscale to Plan 9 had a bug resulting in launching an infinite number of goroutines. Fixing that bug in our
safesocket
IPC package to just boringly using localhost TCP fixed that and now
tailscaled
would run without cras
43557790.article_summary: 本文介绍了Tailscale团队在2025年4月1日愚人节宣布将Tailscale移植到Plan 9操作系统的背后故事。最初，团队认为只需简单调整构建标签和路径即可完成移植，但在实际操作中发现Go编译器对Plan 9的支持已经退化，导致运行时崩溃。经过多番努力，包括修复Go编译器中的Plan 9特殊情况以及解决SSE指令和内存管理问题，最终在2025年3月完成了实际可运行的Plan 9移植版本。团队特别感谢前Go团队成员Russ Cox的帮助，他解决了Plan 9内核中保存和恢复SSE寄存器的问题，使得移植得以成功。最终，Tailscale现在确实能够在Plan 9上运行。

data.author: TaurenHunter
data.article_summary: 一篇由加州大学伯克利分校经济学教授Joe Shapiro撰写的研究论文发现，全球各国对高碳排放的“脏”行业产品征收的进口关税显著低于“清洁”行业产品。这种“环境偏向”存在于多个国家的贸易政策中，导致高污染行业实际上获得了每吨二氧化碳85至120美元的隐性补贴。这一差额远高于经济学家估算的每吨碳排放的社会成本（约40至50美元）。造成这种偏向的原因之一是上游原材料（如钢铁、铝）的生产通常比下游产品（如汽车、手机）更依赖化石燃料，而 lobbying 活动也影响了关税设置。研究指出，调整这一偏向可在不显著影响全球收入的情况下大幅降低碳排放，并可能获得污染行业的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关税在国际贸易中的作用及其对市场公平性的影响

不同观点：
• [perrygeo的观点] 支持关税的理论基础是防止他国通过违反环境或劳工权益来压低价格。例如，美国木材公司需遵守环境法并支付合理工资，而海外竞争者可能无需遵守这些规定，从而以低价冲击市场。关税可以平衡竞争环境，使美国公司无需通过非法或不道德行为参与竞争。然而，该评论者指出，实际情况与此理论相反，各国似乎乐于从境外的剥削中获利。

• [隐含的反对观点] 尽管[perrygeo]支持关税的理论基础，但指出实际效果与预期不符。各国在实践中并未通过关税来抵制剥削，反而可能默许或从中获利。这暗示了关税政策在实际操作中的无效性或矛盾性。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于关税是否能够有效防止市场中的不公平竞争行为。理论上，关税可以作为一种工具来保护本国市场免受不道德商业行为的冲击，但实际操作中，各国可能并未严格执行这一原则。

• 例子中的美国木材公司与海外竞争者的对比，突显了在全球化背景下，不同国家间的法律和道德标准差异如何影响市场竞争。

• 评论还暗示了对全球化经济中道德与经济利益冲突的深层次思考，即各国在追求经济利益时，是否真正关注境外的劳工权益和环境问题。

43573564.article_content:
Business & economics
,
Research
,
Science & environment
Forget carbon tariffs: Existing trade policies give dirty industries a boost
Countries around the world consistently apply lower import taxes on products produced by high-emitting "dirty" industries than “clean” ones
By
Kara Manke
May 4, 2020
Countries around the world consistently apply lower tariffs on products produced by “dirty” industries than by “clean” ones, finds a new analysis. (iStock photo)
In the United States and around the globe, products produced by “dirty” or high-carbon-emitting industries are facing significantly lower import taxes than their cleaner counterparts, finds
a new paper
from the University of California, Berkeley.
Fixing this “environmental bias” in trade policy could significantly lower global carbon emissions, while having little impact on overall global income, argues study author Joe Shapiro, an associate professor of economics and of agriculture and resource economics at UC Berkeley.
“It’s rare to find a systematic pattern that happens in many countries with broadly similar magnitude, but that’s what happens here,” said Shapiro. “This suggests that when countries go negotiate their trade policies, there is scope for that to have important large effects on the environment.”
The analysis was
published online
May 4 as part of the UC Berkeley’s
Energy Institute Working Paper Series
.
The finding comes at a time when many politicians — including 2020 presidential candidate Joe Biden — have proposed implementing higher import taxes, otherwise known as carbon tariffs, on goods produced by dirty industries.
Instead, existing trade policy grants what is essentially an $85 to $120 subsidy to polluting industries per ton of carbon dioxide produced, the study found.
“If you took two arbitrary bundles of goods that showed up in some port around the world, if one of those bundles of goods emitted one additional ton of carbon dioxide to produce, those dirtier goods would face an average of approximately $85 to $120 less in tariffs and in non-tariff barrier obstacles,” Shapiro said.
The approximate “carbon tariff,” or difference between tariffs on low-emitting and high-emitting industries, calculated for various countries around the world. Note that many countries that are considered to have strong environmental protections, such as those in the E.U., also have some of the strongest “environmental biases” in their trade policies, with significantly lower tariffs for dirty industries than for clean industries. (UC Berkeley graphic by Joe Shapiro)
That number is startling, given that many economists estimate that the global “social cost” of carbon emissions — and therefore, the optimal tax on carbon emissions — to be $40 or $50 per ton of carbon dioxide produced.
The significant discrepancy between tariffs on dirty and clean industries is likely due to a factor that economists like to call “upstreamness,” Shapiro found.
Raw goods, like steel and aluminum, are used as precursors to consumer goods, like automobiles and cell phones, and therefore are considered more “upstream” than the end products. The production of upstream raw materials is usually more fossil-fuel intensive than that for their downstream counterparts, which often include “clean” inputs, like software or design.
Powerful lobbying groups, like those representing automobile or technology industries, often push politicians to keep tariffs on raw goods low — so these industries have cheaper access to materials — while advocating for high tariffs on their own products, to protect their consumer bases.
While higher tariffs on dirty industries may impact consumer prices, they are also “one of the few environmental policies I am aware of which appeals to environmentalists and to polluting industries,” Shapiro said.
“Some environmental policies increase the cost of producing pollution-intensive goods, and so pollution-intensive industries lobby against them,” Shapiro said. “This is an environmental policy that protects the dirty industries, so they may lobby for it, and it has the potential to decrease carbon emissions.”
Youtuber econimate explores Shapiro’s findings in this illustrated video.
RELATED INFORMATION
The Environmental Bias of Trade Policy
(Energy Institute Working Paper Series)
International Trade Policies Subsidize Pollution
(Energy Institute Blog)

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ben Eater的计算机项目及其教育意义和实际操作可行性

不同观点：
• [asdefghyk] 认为可以将项目构建在"数字逻辑模拟器"中，提出使用 wire wrap 来简化布线过程，并提到过去使用这种方法的经验。
• [rs186] 对项目持谨慎态度，认为时间和金钱成本高，部件难找，教程过时且存在设计问题，调试过程可能令人沮丧，不适合所有人。
• [JKCalhoun] 支持Ben Eater的项目，认为其视频教程详尽且有教育意义，尤其适合对数字电子有兴趣的人。
• [brucehoult] 指出项目计算机内存极小（16字节），功能有限，但作为可理解的冯·诺依曼计算机仍有教育价值。
• [nanolith] 认为Ben Eater的项目是很好的起点，可以通过修改和扩展提升性能，并指出项目可以作为学习HDL和FPGA的桥梁。
• [apricot] 认为Ben Eater的CPU项目基础但低效，推荐Gigatron作为更强大选择。
• [schoen] 提到有人实现了NAND到Tetris设计，认为其有丰富的资源，可能是不错的选择。
• [giulianopz] 认为这是电子爱好者的必经之路，并分享了其他类似的项目作为参考。
• [roland35] 回忆大学时类似的数字逻辑课程，认为非常有趣并有教育意义。
• [Simon_O_Rourke] 表示从Ben Eater的视频中学到很多，比大学课程更有收获。
• [markshares] 推荐了另一个相关的YouTube频道，认为也具有学习价值。
• [ata_aman] 赞赏Ben Eater的“从零开始构建”系列，认为其视频清晰且内容优质。
• [tsurba] 建议对计算机工作原理感兴趣但不想实际操作的人可以尝试模拟游戏Turing Complete。

补充讨论：
• 项目的时间和金钱成本高，部件难找，教程过时且存在设计问题。
• 项目适合作为学习数字逻辑和FPGA的桥梁，可以通过修改和扩展提升性能。
• 有其他类似项目（如Gigatron和NAND到Tetris设计）也被提及作为替代选择。
• 项目虽然功能有限，但其教育价值和趣味性被广泛认可。

data.title: Supervisors often prefer rule breakers, up to a point
data.author: rustoo
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：规则的制定目的、遵守与打破的合理性以及在不同情境下的处理方式

不同观点：
• 一些评论者认为理解规则制定的背景和目的至关重要，并强调在确保规则制定者会满意的情况下，可以灵活应对规则。例如，[seeknotfind]指出应理解规则的制定原因并确保规则制定者会满意。[yi_xuan]也强调理解规则的目的和影响是关键。

• 另一些评论者指出规则往往是简化的，以适应复杂的情况，因此可能限制了一些好的行为而允许了一些坏的行为。例如，[pdpi]认为简单的规则在复杂情况下不可避免地会有妥协，存在“允许的坏行为”和“禁止的好行为”的空间。[taeric]进一步指出，有目的性地打破规则并不一定是坏事，但需要在主管可接受的范围内。

• 部分评论者分享了实际管理经验，表示更倾向于信任员工的判断和内在动机，而不是严格执行规则。例如，[madrox]提到除非员工表现不佳，否则不会严格执行考勤政策。[jbmsf]则认为制定规则主要是为了防止最坏的情况发生，对于不属于“最坏的人”的员工会有一定的灵活性。

• 还有一些评论者讨论了规则的起源和组织对规则的重视程度对规则打破的影响。例如，[neilv]提出了规则的来源、组织对规则的重视程度以及管理者与组织在规则上的 alignment 等问题，认为这些因素会影响规则打破的合理性和后果。[nitwit005]特别指出在体育界，员工可能被指示去打破联赛规则而不是公司规则。

• 其他一些评论者从实际操作和风险角度讨论了规则打破的利弊。例如，[userbinator]认为规则打破者能带来收益并移除责任。[rblatz]和[ungreased0675]分享了关于体育界中实际案例的观察，指出某些不当行为可能因其带来的控制力和好处而被默许。[terramars]则通过具体例子说明了规则打破在不同领域（如体育和商业）中的不同影响。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论者提到规则打破的文化差异，例如[userbinator]引用了“先行动后求谅解”的俗语，而[jvanderbot]则指出管理者可以通过责备规则打破者并从中获得好处。

• 最后，[__turbobrew__]强调了使命聚焦的重要性，认为理解组织的目标和运作方式是决定何时打破规则的关键。

争议的焦点主要在于规则打破的合理性和后果，尤其是在不同情境和组织文化下的适用性。

data.title: The cultural evolution of distortion in music
data.author: anigbrowl
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： distortion（失真）在音乐中的应用和影响

不同观点：
• Tade0认为，电吉他失真的波形通常接近锯齿波，而不是三角波，除非弦在正中拨动。他还提到失真的音色会根据弹奏技巧和设备的不同而变化，例如不同放大器（如Mesa Boogie）和效果器（如BOSS DS-1）如何通过技术限制产生独特的音色。Tade0还强调了失真在动态和音色变化中的作用。

• Kazinator指出，单音失真（如电吉他独奏）在主流音乐中较快被接受，因为电路技术不断改进。然而，过于刺耳的失真音色仍然是小众的，只在特定音乐风格中（如重金属）得到广泛应用。他还讨论了失真如何影响和声结构，特别是在重金属音乐中通过失真创造出复杂的音调关系。

• Driggs对原文的长篇分析持批评态度，认为其过于学术化，缺乏艺术性表达。Driggs更欣赏如Henry Rollins和Don Was之间的对话，这种更直接、贴近艺术本身的讨论。

• Myself248分享了个人经历，通过播放Pink Floyd的音乐向他人解释失真，并提出了一个理论，即失真吉他声音类似于发动机的声音，象征着自由，这可能是年轻人被摇滚乐吸引的原因之一。

• Drops引用了Brian Eno的话，强调失真是媒介超越其承载能力的标志，是“失败的声音”，这种声音最终会被珍惜和模仿。Drops的观点强调了失真在现代艺术中作为一种突破媒介限制的表现形式。

补充讨论：
• 失真在不同音乐风格中的接受度和应用方式不同，尤其是重金属和爵士/摇滚融合音乐中失真的使用差异。
• 失真音色的变化与设备的技术限制和演奏技巧密切相关，如放大器和效果器的设计如何影响音色。
• 失真作为艺术表现的一部分，其美学价值和象征意义被不同评论者从个人经历和哲学角度进行了探讨。

data.title: Binary Distribution Rebuilds
data.author: JNRowe
data.article_summary: 本文总结了作者在重建Debian和Ubuntu软件包（amd和arm64架构）方面的实验，并与新推出的Reproduce.Debian.net项目进行比较。作者的实验使用最新版软件包进行重建，而Reproduce.Debian.net则使用与发布包相同的构建输入以实现更高的可重现性。作者指出，虽然Reproduce.Debian.net有可能达到100%的可重现性，但还需更进一步，实现“幂等重建”（Idempotent Rebuild），即通过反复重建最终得到一致的档案。当前，由于时间戳和不确定输出等问题，N（重建次数）可能为无穷大，但理想情况是实现N=1。作者计划发布阶段#0的构建产物以进一步实验，但目前尚未取得更多技术进展。

主要讨论点：Debian main 是否能够自我重建以及如何解决其中涉及的非自由固件和未签名二进制文件的问题。

不同观点：
• [yjftsjthsd-h] 认为 Debian main 可能已经进入了一种无法自我重建的状态，主要因为非自由固件和未由 Debian 签名的二进制文件的存在。这些因素可能破坏了 Debian 的可重建性和纯粹性。他提出，如果没有任何非自由包被用作构建输入，可以通过在一个没有 blob（非自由固件）的平台上引导 Guix，并从那里交叉构建 Debian。

• [lrvick] 提供了另一种思路，建议考虑使用具有更严格供应链安全策略的工具，如 Guix，并推荐了 https://stagex.tools/ 作为替代方案，以应对 Debian 目前可能面临的供应链安全问题。

补充讨论：
• [yjftsjthsd-h] 强调了 Debian 重建过程中的 idempotent（幂等性）和 bootstrapped（自举）特性，指出需要解决非自由固件和未签名二进制文件的问题才能实现完全的重建。

• [lrvick] 的回应中隐含了对 Guix 工具链的认可，特别是其在供应链安全方面的严格性，并通过推荐 stagex.tools 提供了一个实际的工具选择。

争议焦点：Debian main 是否已经因为非自由固件和未签名二进制文件的存在而无法自我重建，以及如何有效解决这些问题以确保其重建能力和安全性。

43534143.article_content:
I rebuilt (the top-50 popcon) Debian and Ubuntu packages, on amd and arm64, and
compared the results a couple of months ago
. Since then the
Reproduce.Debian.net
effort has been launched. Unlike my small experiment, that effort is a full-scale rebuild with more architectures. Their goal is to reproduce what is published in the
Debian
archive.
One differences between these two approaches are the build inputs: The Reproduce Debian effort use the same build inputs which were used to build the published packages. I’m using the latest version of published packages for the rebuild.
What does that difference imply? I believe
reproduce.debian.net
will be able to reproduce more of the packages in the archive. If you build a C program using one version of
GCC
you will get some binary output; and if you use a later GCC version you are likely to end up with a different binary output. This is a good thing: we want GCC to evolve and produce better output over time. However it means in order to reproduce the binaries we publish and use, we need to rebuild them using whatever build dependencies were used to prepare those binaries. The conclusion is that we need to use the old GCC to rebuild the program, and this appears to be the Reproduce.Debian.Net approach.
It would be a huge success if the Reproduce.Debian.net effort were to reach 100% reproducibility, and this seems to be within reach.
However I argue that we need go further than that. Being able to rebuild the packages reproducible using older binary packages only begs the question: can we rebuild those older packages? I fear attempting to do so ultimately leads to a need to rebuild 20+ year old packages, with a non-negligible amount of them being illegal to distribute or are unable to build anymore due to bit-rot. We won’t solve
the Trusting Trust concern
if our rebuild effort assumes some initial binary blob that we can no longer build from source code.
I’ve made an illustration of the effort I’m thinking of, to reach something that is stronger than reproducible rebuilds. I am calling this concept a Idempotent Rebuild, which is an old concept that I believe is the
same as John Gilmore has described
many years ago.
The illustration shows how the Debian main archive is used as input to rebuild another “stage #0” archive. This stage #0 archive can be compared with
diffoscope
to the main archive, and all differences are things that would be nice to resolve. The packages in the stage #0 archive is used to prepare a new container image with build tools, and the stage #0 archive is used as input to rebuild another version of itself, called the “stage #1” archive. The differences between stage #0 and stage #1 are also useful to analyse and resolve. This process can be repeated many times. I believe it would be a useful property if this process terminated at some point, where the stage #N archive was identical to the stage #N-1 archive. If this would happen, I label the output archive as an Idempotent Rebuild of the distribution.
How big is N today? The simplest assumption is that it is infinity. Any build timestamp embedded into binary packages will change on every iteration. This will cause the process to never terminate. Fixing embedded timestamps is something that the Reproduce.Debian.Net effort will also run into, and will have to resolve.
What other causes for differences could there be? It is easy to see that generally if some output is not deterministic, such as the sort order of assembler object code in binaries, then the output will be different. Trivial instances of this problem will be caught by the reproduce.debian.net effort as well.
Could there be higher order chains that lead to infinite N? It is easy to imagine the existence of these, but I don’t know how they would look like in practice.
An ideal would be if we could get down to N=1. Is that technically possible? Compare building GCC, it performs an initial stage 0 build using the system compiler to produce a stage 1 intermediate, which is used to build itself again to stage 2. Stage 1 and 2 is compared, and on success (identical binaries), the compilation succeeds. Here N=2. But this is performed using some unknown system compiler that is normally different from the GCC version being built. When rebuilding a binary distribution, you start with the same source versions. So it seems N=1 could be possible.
I’m unhappy to not be able to report any further technical progress now. The next step in this effort is to publish the stage #0 build artifacts in a repository, so they can be used to build stage #1. I already showed that stage #0 was around ~30% reproducible compared to the official binaries, but I didn’t save the artifacts in a reusable repository. Since the official binaries were not built using the latest versions, it is to be expected that the reproducibility number is low. But what happens at stage #1? The percentage should go up: we are now compare the rebuilds with an earlier rebuild, using the sa

Innovation and Tech

Introduction
Magic and Espionage at CIA
The Master of Deception, Harry Houdini
A Spy for America?
The worldâs most famous magician, Harry Houdini, was known as a celebrity conjurer, a practitioner of escape magic, and a master illusionist. Heâs had an enduring legacy on the magical arts since his untimely demise on Halloween Day, 1926. Thatâs why October 31
st
is known in magical circles as âNational Magic Dayâ or simply âHoudini Day.â
In honor of this legendary magician, weâre exploring the effect magic, and even Houdini, has had in the realms of intelligence and espionage.
Harry Houdini, courtesy of the Library of Congress
It may surprise people to learn that Houdiniâs magical techniques have influenced generations of clandestine officers. We even had a former CIA deputy director who was a magician himself!
But was Houdini more than just an influential figure?
Was he ever a practitioner in the art of espionage?
Was he a spy?
To answer these questions, we must first delve into the mystery of the missing magic manuals of Langley and the CIAâs first magician, John Mulholland.
Vintage poster for Harry Houdini show, courtesy of the Library of Congress.
Magic and Espionage at CIA
âMagic and espionage are really kindred arts,â or so wrote former CIA Deputy Director McLaughlin, an amateur magician himself, in the forward to the book, âThe Official C.I.A. Manual of Trickery and Deceptionâ by H. Keith Melton and Robert Wallace.
This book, created from two long-lost training guides designed to teach Agency officers how to integrate elements of the magicianâs craft into clandestine operations, revealed that the CIAâs connection to the world of magic was decades old.
In the 1950s, as part of the MKULTRA project, the Agency hired magician John Mulholland to teach young officers techniques of deception suitable for the field, such as smuggling assets out of East Germany during the Cold War in vehicles that resembled the magic boxes used in stage illusions.
As part of his contract, Mulholland prepared two training manuals; âSome Operational Applications of the Art of Deceptionâ and âRecognition Signals.â
In 1973, when then-CIA Director Richard Helms ordered the destruction of all documents associated with the MKULTRA program, the manuals were thought to be gone forever.
Then, in 2007 while going through some unrelated documents, Robert Wallace, a former director of the CIAâs Office of Technical Services, discovered references to the manuals and tracked down poor-quality copies of each that had somehow escaped the shredder.
Believing that the manuals merited publication in full, Wallace conferred with his co-author, intelligence historian and collector Keith Melton, to produce âThe Official C.I.A. Manual of Trickery and Deception,â which included illustrations of stage deception techniques, such as Harry Houdiniâs walk through a wall.
In fact, many of Houdiniâs magical escape techniques are discussed in the now declassified manuals, as they have influenced later generations of clandestine officers as well as spy gadgetry developed during the Cold War.
According to the Trickery and Deception book, concealment devises like magic coins and the hollow Mokana shoe used by Houdini for hiding escape tools became popular among spies throughout the Cold War era.
Even the Office of Strategic Services, the CIAâs WWII predecessor, was inspired by Houdini when they created tiny tools that mirrored those first used by the magician in his concealed escape kits.
Itâs no wonder then that many historians of magic and intelligence have found themselves pondering the question: Was Harry Houdiniâ¦
a spy?
Hungarian born magician and escapologist Harry Houdini (1874 – 1926) being fitted into an escape proof suit.   (Photo by MPI/Getty Images)
The Master of Deception, Harry Houdini
Since Houdiniâs death, there has been an on-going debate among historians as to whether or not Houdini was ever a âspy.â
The greatestÂ and most recent kerfuffle was theÂ publication in 2006 of âThe Secret Life of Houdini: The Making of Americaâs First Superheroâ by William Kalush and Larry Sloman, who conducted exhaustive research into the history of magic, eventually creating a fully text-searchable database of 700,000 pages of material, which contains thousands of references to Houdini.
Kalush and Sloman posit that the only reason Houdini would abruptly leave the United States in 1900, when he had finally achieved notorietyâand a paycheck equivalent to $45,000 a weekâwas because he was engaged in espionage. Houdini was rumored to be providing the German police with information about wanted criminals, as well as unspecified information to Scotland Yard Superintendent William Melville, monitoring anarchists in Russia, and helping the U.S. Secret Service with their anti-counterfeiting mission.

data.author: jvkersch
data.article_summary:
该仓库提供了一个简化的去噪扩散模型（Denoising Diffusion）的PyTorch实现，代码主要参考了《The Annotated Diffusion》和Phil Wang的扩散模型库，并进行了重构以使逻辑更清晰。项目目标是帮助理解扩散模型的基础构建块，适用于学习及未来项目。代码结构包括：  
- **funct_diffusion.py**：包含正向和反向扩散过程的必要函数。  
- **cls_dataset.py**：包含数据相关的类和函数，使用了单一类别的数据增强。  
- **cls_model.py**：包含模型实现，基本复制了《The Annotated Diffusion》的模型结构。  
- **main_train_diffusion.py**：用于训练扩散模型。  
- **main_generate_images.py**：使用训练好的模型生成图像。  

生成图像的质量还有提升空间，更多复杂方法可参考Phil Wang的扩散模型库。所需库包括torch、torchvision、datasets、PIL和numpy。

参考文献：  
[1] Song and Ermon, Generative Modeling by Estimating Gradients of the Data Distribution  
[2] Ho et al., Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models  

许可证：MIT许可证

Simple Denoising Diffusion
This repository contains a bare-bone implementation of denoising diffusion [1,2] in PyTorch, with majority of its code taken from
The Annotated Diffusion
and
Phil Wang's diffusion repository
. Both resources are great to get started with diffusion models but they were still a bit convoluted for me when I first started learning about diffusion models so I refactored majority of
The Annotated Diffusion
's implementation and made a bare-bone implementation with functions and classes logically separated into different files as a learning exercise. My goal was to understand the building blocks of diffusion models in order to use them in some upcoming projects. I'm sharing this repo in hopes that my exercise will be useful for you in understanding more complex implementations.
Code Overview
Code is organized under src folder as follows:
funct_diffusion.py
- Contains all necessary functions for forward and backward diffusion process, including the scheduler.
cls_dataset.py
- Contains data-related functions and classes. I used a single class (n01443537 - Carassius auratus - Goldfish) with some augmentations (e.g., rotations and flips), that's why generated images have several upside down fishes.
cls_model.py
- Contains the model. The model in this repo is basically a copy paste of
The Annotated Diffusion
's implementation, except for dim_mults=(1, 2, 4, 8) and channe=3 (RGB).
main_train_diffusion.py
- I wanted to separate training and generation into two different files to digest what parameter is needed for what. This file is used to train the diffusion model.
main_generate_images.py
- Generates images using the trained model.
Examples
Examples from the dataset:
Examples generated by the diffusion model (rotations are because of the data augmentation, it's hilarious though):
Example diffusion process:
Outro
As you can see, generated images are not as crisp as those from the dataset. There are many improvements that can be incorporated to improve the image quality, with each of those adding more to the complexity.
Phil Wang's diffusion repository
is a great place to discover some of those methods.

主要讨论点：技术社区中的专业术语（jargon）和缩写对新手的可接近性以及其影响

不同观点：
• **don-code**：认为软件各领域都有自己的共享词汇，有助于提高沟通效率。一些社区（如DevOps、Python、Ruby、Rust）对新手很友好，使用易懂的语言。然而，安全和网络社区则充斥着缩略词，且部分从业者以知晓这些术语为荣，形成了不友好的氛围。
• **kotaKat**：认为虽然专业术语是平台力量的一部分，但需要有意识地去教。许多时候解释只停留在“是什么”，而没有深入“为什么”。并且，一些“守门人”式的态度阻碍了新手学习。
• **pjmlp**：认为技术领域充斥缩略词是普遍现象，并不局限于某个特定领域。
• **GianFabien**：指出年轻的技术人员更喜欢用AI、ML、GPT等流行缩略词，忽视了如COBOL、Java等“古老”技术。这反映了某种文化现象，可能让新手难以接触到传统但重要的技术知识。
• **classichasclass**：指出IBM词汇不仅仅限于大型主机，IBM的中端系统也使用类似的术语，如“IPL”。
• **Frummy**：提到随着AI的发展，现在学习这些专业术语和概念可能比过去容易得多。
• **rbanffy**：提供了一个IBM文档链接，帮助理解相关术语。
• **jgalt212**：幽默地指出文章未提到“WENUS”这个术语，暗示对某些内容的遗漏。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：技术社区中使用专业术语和缩略词的合理性。一部分人认为这些术语有助于高效沟通，另一部分人则认为它们形成了新手进入的障碍，尤其是在某些特定社区（如安全和网络）。
- **文化现象**：年轻技术人员更倾向于使用当前流行的技术术语，而忽视或不了解传统技术，这可能影响知识的传承和社区的包容性。
- **教学问题**：强调了不仅要解释“是什么”，还要解释“为什么”，以帮助新手更好地理解和融入技术社区。
- **具体例子**：如DevOps、Python等社区对新手友好，而安全和网络社区则存在不友好的现象。IBM系统中“IPL”等术语的使用范围也被讨论。

总体而言，评论主要围绕技术社区的专业术语和缩略词对新手的影响，以及如何更好地进行知识传承和社区建设。

- **文化现象**：年轻技术人员更倾向于使用当前流行的技术术语，而忽视或不了解传统技术，这可能影响知识的传承和社区的包容性。
- **教学问题**：强调了不仅要解释“是什么”，还要解释“为什么”，以帮助新手更好地理解和融入技术社区。
- **具体例子**：如DevOps、Python等社区对新手友好，而安全和网络社区则存在不友好的现象。IBM系统中“IPL”等术语的使用范围也被讨论。

总体而言，评论主要围绕技术社区的专业术语和缩略词对新手的影响，以及如何更好地进行知识传承和社区建设。

When
Grab
laid off 1,000 of its employees
in mid-2023, CEO Anthony Tan said the $19bn Singapore
fintech
was trying to "rebalance [its] resources." Little was revealed about the specifics at the time, including the closure of an expensive office that has slipped under the radar ever since.
Click here to follow our new WhatsApp channel, and get instant news updates straight to your phone 📱
.
Sources close to the matter, speaking anonymously, confirmed that Grab closed its
Seattle
office as part of the layoffs. The location was
opened in 2016
and aimed to grow to
at least 140 people
within two years of opening. The office was home to some senior Grab staff, including
Mark Porter,
CTO of its transport business (although he left prior to the layoffs).
The layoffs were thought to affect the vast majority of staff, although insiders say "a few people were retained due to their domain knowledge" in a
remote capacity.
Grab's Seattle staff were
costly
. While firmwide staff costs per head in 2023 were $104k, engineers on Levels.fyi reported an average total compensation of $271.5k in Seattle. Multiple engineers reported salaries above $300k.
In the fintech's 2024
20-F form
, filed with the SEC eight months after the layoffs, Grab still listed Seattle as one of its ten (now eight) tech hubs. However, in its most recent 20-F, Seattle was removed. Its Taipei tech hub was also removed from the list, though that hub's fate is unclear.
"The U.S. office was nothing more than a façade," one of Grab's former Seattle software engineers told us, adding that there was, "no real long-term commitment to its employees." The employee claimed that Grab offered little support to people with visa complications arising from the layoffs.
There are also claims that Grab pressured employees to remove social media posts complaining about the layoffs by putting their severance packages at risk, although this is unconfirmed.
Shifting roles across to
lower cost locations
has been a trend in fintech in recent years. Prior to the layoffs, Grab jobs in
Malaysia
outnumbered jobs in Singapore
ten to one
. There are still more Grab jobs in Malaysia than
Singapore
today, although the difference isn't nearly as big.
Grab did not respond to multiple requests for comment.

data.title: Show HN: Slipstream – A Python library for stateful stream processing
data.author: menziess
data.article_summary: Slipstream是一个简化有状态流应用程序开发的数据流模型框架。它具有以下特点：简化并行处理和源到接收器的映射，允许任意代码而不受限于抽象，通过优化和可配置的默认设置快速启动。它可以消费任何可转化为异步可迭代对象的源（如Kafka、流API），并将数据缓存到任何可调用对象（如Kafka、RocksDB、API）。开发者可以使用常规Python代码执行任意有状态操作，如连接、聚合和过滤，还能检测依赖流中断、暂停相关流或发送修正。通过基本Python构建块，可以轻松实现定时器等功能。例如，使用`slipstream.handle`绑定源和接收器到处理函数，启动数据流。Slipstream简化了有状态流应用的开发流程。

Slipstream provides a data-flow model to simplify development of stateful streaming applications.

data.title: Install script does rm -RF /usr for Ubuntu
data.author: tyleo
data.article_summary: 该报告描述了一个由安装脚本中的错误引发的严重问题。在Ubuntu系统上运行该脚本时，由于脚本第351行多了一个空格，导致命令`rm -rf /usr /lib/nvidia-current/xorg/xorg`错误地执行了`rm -rf /usr`，删除了系统中的`/usr`目录，造成数据丢失。用户不得不重新安装Linux系统以恢复。报告建议立即修复该问题，去掉多余的空格以避免严重后果。这个问题引起了广泛关注和讨论。

data.author: vyrotek
data.article_summary: 文章主要指出，大约20年前，海外制造更便宜的优势已经消失。企业离开美国主要是因为海外的劳动力优势，以及民主党和共和党制定的大量法规，导致在美国制造几乎不可能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：国际贸易和制造业成本，特别是关于桌面游戏在中美之间生产的选择及相关关税影响。

不同观点：
• **neilwilson**：认为在中国生产游戏的成本以人民币计算，而不是美元，且当前汇率需要从1:7调整到1:14，才能使中国继续成为可行的生产来源。他还提到中国主权财富基金需要更慷慨地提供人民币。

• **stevenwoo**：认为文章最后的建议（在美国建立制造业）比2025年那些掌权者提出的策略更具说服力，特别是在桌面游戏领域。

• **Gollapalli**：质疑在美国印刷和出版这些游戏的实际成本，认为主要材料不过是层压纸板和一些树脂件，质疑高成本的合理性。

• **4ndrewl**：指出文章揭示了关税支持者所传播的虚假二分法，选项不仅仅是“外国工作 vs 美国工作”，而是“部分国外生产 vs 全部美国生产 vs 根本不生产”。自由贸易让新产品和低价产品得以存在。

• **Yeul**：认为世界其他国家会绕过美国继续贸易，贸易不会因为某些政治决策而停止。并以Netflix上韩剧和日剧为例，说明创意产业也在发生变化。

• **nine_zeros**：提到软件公司的成本将大幅上升，因为笔记本电脑、办公椅、桌子、电缆等成本增加。在这种情况下，可能完全在国外开发，然后以一次性关税在美国销售更划算。

• **alephnerd**：澄清这是货物关税，不直接影响服务进口如游戏、视觉特效或外包软件。并在编辑后纠正自己，说明文章是关于桌面游戏，而非电子游戏。

• **whoiscroberts**：认为美国的贸易伙伴应降低关税/利润，使美国进口商和出版商能够获得合理利润，或者接受订单减少的事实。

补充讨论：
• 评论之间的争议焦点在于中美生产成本和关税对行业的影响，特别是桌面游戏行业。部分评论者如neilwilson和4ndrewl讨论了生产成本和关税之间的复杂关系，而Yeul和nine_zeros则更关注全球贸易环境的变化及其对美国的影响。stevenwoo和Gollapalli则对在美国生产的可行性和实际成本提出了具体看法。

• **Gollapalli**：质疑在美国印刷和出版这些游戏的实际成本，认为主要材料不过是层压纸板和一些树脂件，质疑高成本的合理性。

• **4ndrewl**：指出文章揭示了关税支持者所传播的虚假二分法，选项不仅仅是“外国工作 vs 美国工作”，而是“部分国外生产 vs 全部美国生产 vs 根本不生产”。自由贸易让新产品和低价产品得以存在。

• **Yeul**：认为世界其他国家会绕过美国继续贸易，贸易不会因为某些政治决策而停止。并以Netflix上韩剧和日剧为例，说明创意产业也在发生变化。

• **nine_zeros**：提到软件公司的成本将大幅上升，因为笔记本电脑、办公椅、桌子、电缆等成本增加。在这种情况下，可能完全在国外开发，然后以一次性关税在美国销售更划算。

• **alephnerd**：澄清这是货物关税，不直接影响服务进口如游戏、视觉特效或外包软件。并在编辑后纠正自己，说明文章是关于桌面游戏，而非电子游戏。

• **whoiscroberts**：认为美国的贸易伙伴应降低关税/利润，使美国进口商和出版商能够获得合理利润，或者接受订单减少的事实。

补充讨论：
• 评论之间的争议焦点在于中美生产成本和关税对行业的影响，特别是桌面游戏行业。部分评论者如neilwilson和4ndrewl讨论了生产成本和关税之间的复杂关系，而Yeul和nine_zeros则更关注全球贸易环境的变化及其对美国的影响。stevenwoo和Gollapalli则对在美国生产的可行性和实际成本提出了具体看法。

data.title: Teen with 4.0 GPA who built the viral Cal AI app was rejected by 15 universities
data.author: impish9208
data.article_summary: Zach Yadegari, a high school teen and co-founder of the AI calorie-tracking app Cal AI, was rejected by 15 out of 18 top colleges despite having a 4.0 GPA and a high ACT score. He believes his essay, which discussed his initial reluctance to attend college and his success as a self-taught coder, may have been the issue. Yadegari had previously sold a web gaming company for $100,000 and his current app has been downloaded over 1 million times. His essay emphasized his desire to experience college life and learn from people, not just online resources. After his tweet about the rejections went viral, many criticized his essay as arrogant, while others blamed the college admission system. Yadegari, reflecting on the response, realized that success is not just about financial achievements but also relationships and community involvement. He was accepted by Georgia Tech, University of Texas, and University of Miami.

43576589.article_content:
Zach Yadegari,
the high school teen co-founder of Cal AI
, is being hammered
with comments on X
after he revealed that out of 18 top colleges he applied to, he was rejected by 15.
Yadegari says that he got a 4.0 GPA and nailed a 34 score on his ACT (above 31 is considered a top score). His problem, he’s sure — as are tens of thousands of commenters on X — was his essay.
As TechCrunch reported last month, Yadegari is the co-founder of the viral AI calorie-tracking app Cal AI, which Yadegari says is generating millions in revenue, on a $30 million annual recurring revenue track. While we can’t verify that revenue claim, the app stores do say the app was downloaded over 1 million times and has tens of thousands of positive reviews.
Cal AI was actually his second success. He sold his previous web gaming company for $100,000, he said.
Yadegari hadn’t intended on going to college. He and his co-founder had already spent a summer at a hacker house in San Francisco building their prototype, and he thought he would become a classic (if not cliché) college-dropout tech entrepreneur.
But the time in the hacker house taught him that if he didn’t go to college, he would be forgoing a big part of his young adult life. So he opted for more school.
And his essay said about as much.
He posted the whole thing on X. It repeatedly said how he never planned on going to college and documented his experience making ever more money as a self-taught coder. He wrote how VCs and mentors reinforced the idea that he didn’t need college.
All until he had an epiphany: “In my rejection of the collegiate path, I had unwittingly bound myself to another framework of expectations: the archetypal dropout founder. Instead of schoolteachers, it was VCs and mentors steering me toward a direction that was still not my own,” he wrote.
College would help him “elevate the work I have always done” so he now wanted to learn from humans, not just books and YouTube.
His penultimate paragraph declared, “Through college, I will contribute to and grow within that larger whole, empowering me to leave an even greater lasting, positive impact on the world.”
Despite the grades, test scores, and real-world achievements, he was rejected by Stanford, MIT, Harvard, Columbia, Princeton, Duke, and Cornell, among others. He was, however, accepted by Georgia Tech, University of Texas, and University of Miami.
Still, his tweet about the many rejections went viral, with over 22 million views, more than 2,700 retweets and upwards of 3,600 comments.
Many of the comments blasted the essay as “arrogant,”
saying that was the problem
.
Others blasted the college acceptance system as the problem (with
all the usual criticisms
there).
Probably the more insightful comments were
the ones pointing
out that colleges are looking for candidates who seem thirsty for education and will likely graduate. His essay read like he had barely convinced himself to attend.
Even Y Combinator’s Garry Tan
weighed in on X
, not with feedback for Yadegari, but with his own “confession” that he was also widely rejected and waitlisted on his college apps “because I rewrote my essays after reading Ayn Rand’s ‘The Fountainhead.’”  and’s Objectivism philosophy appears to be a permanently controversial topic, it seems. (Tan, however, did get into and attended Stanford.)
Yadegari tells TechCrunch that he’s still figuring out his next steps but was fascinated by the response his X post received. “It was interesting to see many different perspectives, but ultimately, I’ll never know exactly why I was turned down. At the end of the day, when I wrote my essay, I hoped admissions offices would perceive me as authentic because that’s all I ever want to be.”
Yadegari also says he’s come to realize that business success isn’t the greatest achievement of his 17-year-old life. Having obtained some of that, “I realized that life was not just about financial success,” he said, “it is about relationships, and about being a part of a larger community.”

data.title: Restructuring Announcement
data.author: markx2
data.article_summary: 2025年4月2日，Automattic CEO马特·穆伦维格宣布公司进行重组，以确保长期稳定发展。尽管收入增长，但面临激烈竞争和技术快速变革，公司需要提高生产力、盈利能力和投资能力。重组目标包括增强敏捷性、打破效率低下的壁垒、专注于产品质量及确保财务稳健。此次重组将导致约16%的员工被裁减，被影响员工将获得包括遣散费、保留公司笔记本电脑及就业资源在内的支持。公司承诺清晰、 compassionately沟通，并为离职员工提供心理和实际支持。穆伦维格鼓励留下来的员工感谢离职同事，并共同努力推动公司发展。未来几周将分享更多前进路径和公司强化计划。

43559855.article_content:
Restructuring Announcement
Automattic
·
April 2, 2025
Earlier today, CEO Matt Mullenweg shared with Automattic employees the following message.
I have had to make difficult decisions to protect Automattic’s long-term future. This post will outline why the changes are happening and the next steps in our organizational restructuring. I wish to be transparent and acknowledge immediately that this will be difficult news to hear. We will do everything to ensure that all Automatticians, those staying and those leaving, are supported.
Why We’re Making Changes
We have reached an important crossroads. While our revenue continues to grow, Automattic operates in a highly competitive market, and technology is evolving at unprecedented levels. To support our customers and products, we must improve our productivity, profitability, and capacity to invest.
As difficult as this decision has been, we are restructuring the company to:
Become more agile and responsive.
Break down silos that have created inefficiencies.
Focus on product quality, doing fewer things better.
Ensure a viable financial model for long-term success.
What This Means
This restructuring will result in an approximately 16% workforce reduction. HR will email those impacted to inform them they will leave Automattic with financial and support benefits.
Supporting Those Affected
This process is complex with Automatticians in 90 countries, but we’re committed to communicating clearly and compassionately. Colleagues who will be leaving will receive:
A comprehensive package covering severance pay and benefits.
Retention of company laptops.
Job placement resources.
They also have our enduring gratitude for their time with the company.
Looking Forward
Automattic has multiple products with world-touching potential in WordPress and beyond. I’m confident we will come out of this situation in a better position, poised to create a vibrant, profitable, well-designed company that will continue our mission to democratize the internet. I would ask that you take a moment to thank and appreciate the efforts of your teammates who have left the company, reflect on how you will move forward as an individual and Automattician, and join me in the vital work we have in front of us. I recognize this is a difficult time. In the coming weeks, we’ll share more about our path forward and how we’ll work together to strengthen our company.
We understand that you may wish to access support and discuss this with those close to you. I’d like to remind you that Automattic partners with Workplace Options, which provides emotional and practical well-being support if you seek advice from an external provider.
[links to resources for employees, redacted]
As always, your HR Wranglers are here to talk with you and support you.

• [gwalkerux] 介绍了自己在前端和全栈开发方面的经验，特别是React、Electron和WordPress开发，并提到自己在可访问性合规方面的专业知识。

• [saulthompson92] 强调自己的全栈和基础设施经验，包括前端的TypeScript、React，后端的Python、Node.js，以及基础设施的AWS和Terraform。

• [hnjobsdustybit] 突出自己的全栈开发经验，特别是在Rust、Ruby、Elixir和React方面的技能，并提到自己在维护大型Rails应用和参与电子商务业务方面的背景。

补充讨论：
• 技术多样性：从业者们展示了广泛的技术栈，从JavaScript/TypeScript的全栈应用，到特定领域的技术如Lisp、Golang、Swift和Rust。
• 团队和领导能力：多位从业者强调了自己的团队管理和领导经验，如[arctangos]、[irishmansevilla]和[hnjobsdustybit]，这表明技术领导力在这些职位中的重要性。
• 远程工作偏好：大多数从业者表示愿意远程工作或偏好远程工作，如[Scenic0573]、[a13x57]、[whatamidoingyo]和[gwalkerux]。
• 项目经验：许多从业者提供了自己的项目经验和作品链接，展示了他们在实际项目中的能力，如[Layogtima]的Space Elevator项目和[sinisamikulic]的movieo.me和yourmonthly.app。

争议焦点：
• 技术栈选择：不同的技术栈选择和偏好可能在从业者之间引发讨论，例如Rust与Rails的对比，或者Golang与Node.js的优劣。
• 远程工作与团队合作：一些从业者强调了远程工作的优势，而另一些则提到了团队管理和面对面工作的经验，这可能引发对远程工作效率和团队合作模式的讨论。

data.title: AI masters Minecraft: DeepMind program finds diamonds without being taught
data.author: bglazer
data.article_summary: 研究人员开发了一种名为Dreamer的人工智能系统，能够在《Minecraft》游戏中自主收集钻石，而无需人类指导。这是AI领域的一个重大突破，因为收集钻石需要多个复杂步骤，包括探索环境、收集资源和制作工具。Dreamer通过构建周围环境的模型并利用强化学习进行自我改进，成功完成了这一任务。其关键在于Dreamer能"想象"未来场景，预测不同行动的潜在奖励，从而做出决策。这种能力不仅在游戏中有效，还有望应用于现实世界的机器人互动学习。该研究发表在《Nature》期刊上，标志着通用人工智能系统发展的重要一步。

Minecraft
is among the world’s most popular video games and has 100 million monthly active users.
Credit: Mojang Studios
An artificial intelligence (AI) system has for the first time figured out how to collect diamonds in the hugely popular video game
Minecraft
— a difficult task requiring multiple steps — without being shown how to play. Its creators say the system, called Dreamer, is a step towards machines that can generalize knowledge learn in one domain to new situations, a
major goal of AI
.
“Dreamer marks a significant step towards general AI systems,” says Danijar Hafner, a computer scientist at Google DeepMind in San Francisco, California. “It allows AI to understand its physical environment and also to self-improve over time, without a human having to tell it exactly what to do.” Hafner and his colleagues describe
Dreamer
in a study in
Nature
published on 2 April
1
.
In
Minecraft
, players explore a virtual 3D world containing a variety of terrains, including forests, mountains, deserts and swamps. Players use the world’s resources to create objects, such as chests, fences and swords — and collect items, among the most prized of which are diamonds.
Importantly, says Hafner, no two experiences are the same. “Every time you play
Minecraft
, it’s a new, randomly generated world,” he says. This makes it useful for challenging an AI system that researchers want to be able to generalize from one situation to the next. “You have to really understand what’s in front of you; you can’t just memorize a specific strategy,” he says.
Diamonds are among
Minecraft
’s most prized rewards — but finding them takes a series of complex steps.
Credit: Mojang Studios
Collecting a diamond is “a very hard task”, says computer scientist Jeff Clune at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver, Canada, who was part of a separate team that trained a program to
find diamonds using videos of human play
2
. “There is no question this represents a major step forward for the field.”
Diamonds are forever
AI
researchers have focused on finding diamonds
, says Hafner, because it requires a series of complicated steps, including finding trees and breaking them down to gather wood, which players can use to build a crafting table.
AI takes on popular Minecraft game in machine-learning contest
This, together with more wood, can be used to make a wooden pickaxe — and so on, until players have assembled the correct tools to collect a diamond, which is buried deep underground. “There’s a long chain of these milestones, and so, it requires very deep exploration,” he says.
Previous attempts to get AI systems to collect diamonds relied on using videos of human play
2
or researchers leading systems through the steps.
By contrast, Dreamer explores everything about the game on its own, using a trial-and-error technique called reinforcement learning — it identifies actions that are likely to beget rewards, repeats them and discards others. Reinforcement learning underpins some
major advances in AI
. But previous programs were specialists — they could not apply knowledge in new domains from scratch.
DeepMind’s Dreamer AI played repeated runs in
Minecraft
to learn how to collect diamonds.
Courtesy of Danijar Hafner
Build me a world model
Key to Dreamer’s success, says Hafner, is that it builds a model of its surroundings and uses this ‘world model’ to ‘imagine’ future scenarios and guide decision-making. Rather like our own abstract thoughts, the world model is not an exact replica of its surroundings. But it allows the Dreamer agent to try things out and predict the potential rewards of different actions using less computation than would be needed to complete those actions in
Minecraft
. “The world model really equips the AI system with the ability to imagine the future,” says Hafner.
This ability could also help to create robots that can learn to interact in the real world — where the costs of trial and error are much higher than in a video game, says Hafner.
Testing Dreamer on the diamond challenge was an afterthought. “We built this whole algorithm without that in mind,” says Hafner. But it occurred to the team that it was the ideal way to test whether its algorithm could work, out of the box, on an unfamiliar task.
The Minecraft virtual world consists of multiple different terrains, from swamps and deserts to farms and villages.

data.title: Mozilla launching “Thundermail” email service to take on Gmail, Microsoft 365
data.author: bentobean
data.article_summary: Mozilla正在通过推出Thundermail和Thunderbird Pro，将其开源电子邮件客户端Thunderbird转变为一个全面的通信平台，以与Gmail和Microsoft 365等竞争。Thunderbird Pro包括Appointment（预约工具）、Send（基于Firefox Send的重建版）和Thunderbird Assist（一个本地处理的AI写作工具）。Thundermail是一个使用开源Stalwart堆栈的电子邮件托管服务，用户可在thundermail.com和tb.pro域名之间选择。尽管Mozilla计划最终对部分功能收费，但未来将提供有限制的免费 tier。Mozilla的目标是通过强调隐私和用户尊重等开源价值观，在竞争中脱颖而出。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mozilla推出的Thundermail电子邮件服务及其相关问题

不同观点：
• 对Mozilla长期承诺的担忧：[mmooss]表示担心Mozilla是否能在5-10年内持续提供该服务，尤其是对非技术用户而言，更换电子邮件地址并不理想。虽然有人指出，如果用户能自带域名，技术用户可以保留地址，但对非技术用户来说这并不现实。
• 对产品优化和收费的期待：[ttoinou]希望Thunderbird能支持处理大量电子邮件并优化搜索功能，甚至愿意为此付费，因为这对于商业用户非常重要。
• 对新技术的兴趣：[solarkraft]认为使用开源Stalwart栈是很好的消息，使得JMAP兼容供应商增加，并期待新的web前端开发。
• 对Mozilla及其新服务的信任问题：[inetknght]和[evolve2k]提到过去Mozilla在EULA和TOS上的问题以及信任危机，表示不会使用其新服务。而[mentalgear]则表示支持Mozilla的隐私保护服务，并对其邮件掩码功能有积极评价。

补充讨论：
• 对服务细节的关注：[gruez]对Thundermail与Fastmail或Protonmail的比较，以及是否具备端到端加密等功能提出疑问，担心Mozilla可能只是与其它服务商合作并收取版权费用。
• 对域名选择的质疑：[tianqi]对Thundermail提供的域名选择表示怀疑，认为这些域名不适合电子邮件业务。
• 对Mozilla新服务的乐观态度：[abidhusain]和[theandrewbailey]对Mozilla推出注重隐私的电子邮件服务表示欢迎，认为这是市场中的一股积极力量。
• 对现有问题的不满：[the__alchemist]提到Thunderbird的搜索功能存在问题，无法找到应显示的邮件。
• 对服务发布方式的批评：[tristan957]指出讨论中存在对MZLA Technologies和Mozilla Corporation的混淆，呼吁聚焦于服务本身。
• 对Mozilla使命的质疑：[Y_Y]对Mozilla的开放源代码和隐私保护使命表示怀疑，认为其使命在过去多年中已被侵蚀。

争议焦点：
• Mozilla的信任问题及其新服务的长期可行性。
• Thunderbird的技术优化和收费模式的合理性。
• 新服务在隐私保护和市场竞争中的定位和优势。

(Image credit: Mozilla)
Mozilla takes on Gmail, Microsoft 365 with range of new features
Thunderbird Pro includes Appointment, Send and Thundermail
A new AI writing tool is also coming with local processing
Mozilla is turning its Thunderbird open source
email client
into a full communications platform with the launch of Thundermail and Thunderbird Pro.
The expansion of Mozilla's email services aims to compete with rival ecosystems like Gmail and
Microsoft
365, which are more rich in features, except Mozilla’s offering stands out for its
open source
values of privacy, freedom, transparency and user respect.
“Thunderbird loses users each day to rich ecosystems that are both clients and services,” Ryan Sipes, Managing Director for Product Thunderbird
confirmed
as he expressed the ‘why’ behind Thunderbird’s expansion.
Thunderbird is about to get an overhaul
The Thunderbird
database
says its number of active monthly installs has dropped from 17.7 million in late December 2020 to 16.2 million in late March 2025, with the mail app struggling to keep up with the industry’s main players like Gmail.
With the launch of Thunderbird Pro, Mozilla is adding Thunderbird Appointment, a new scheduling tool for sharing calendar links; Thunderbird Send, a rebuild of the discontinued Firefox Send; and Thunderbird Assist, a new AI-powered writing tool enabled via a partnership with Flower AI that is intended to do the processing locally to eliminate privacy concerns.
The final launch will be Thundermail, an email hosting service using the open-source Stalwart stack. Usrs will be able to pick between thundermail.com and tb.pro domains.
Apart from consistent community contributors who will be able to get early access for free, Sipes confirmed Mozilla would ultimately end up charging for the features, such as Send which requires storage, an expensive commodity.

data.title: Are people bad at their jobs or are the jobs just bad?
data.author: moonka
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：工作环境、劳动质量和经济模式对劳资双方的影响

不同观点：
• [rqtwteye] 认为现代工作环境对员工施加了过多压力，导致他们没有足够的时间和精力做好工作。他怀念90年代软件开发时有更多时间进行实验和学习。他强调员工需要一定的空间和自由，才能产出优质工作，并将谷歌曾经的“20%时间”作为正面例子。

• [brudgers] 强调了零工经济对工人的负面影响，包括无法在公司内晋升、无法建立同事网络，甚至可能与同事竞争工作。零工工作相较于有固定岗位的“死胡同工作”更加不利。

• [ryandrake] 指出评论者往往将自己的工作经历投射到文章上，但文章更多关注的是非技术性和半技术性服务/零工工作者，如送货司机、家具组装工等。这些工作岗位通常待遇差、员工不开心且技能不足，陷入一种“纳什均衡”状态。

• [Uzmanali] 分享了自己对零工平台的失望经历，工人迟到、无法遵循指示且中途离开。他认为这些平台不支持高技能、高薪酬的工人，更多关注廉价和便利，导致服务质量差。相比之下，他更愿意雇佣本地专业人士。

• [thi2] 描述了在超市看到老年员工被迫从事低技能工作的情景，质疑这种现象，并指出顾客可以自己处理一些简单任务，无需员工代劳。

• [zw123456] 分享了自己在科技行业45年的工作经验，强调了面对恐惧的重要性，并鼓励不要害怕与众不同或表现出自己的个性。

• [owenversteeg] 同意“低薪低质”的观点，并进一步指出工作缺乏尊重，员工被视为机器中的齿轮，工作环境缺乏人情味且短期化。

• [nixpulvis] 提到服务业整体质量下降，并认为低工资导致员工不满和粗心大意，这种情绪在服务行业中蔓延。

• [jwr] 认为问题不在于工作本身，而在于工作态度。他以日本为例，指出即使是最低级的岗位，员工也会表现出极高的奉献精神，强调“做或不做”的态度。

• [cadamsdotcom] 指出美国的劳动法过时且执行不力，公司为了盈利可能会剥削员工。他认为需要政府干预，以确保工人获得合理报酬和工作条件。

• [l0new0lf-G] 认为文章提出的通过市场自我调节来解决问题的观点不现实，指出自2008年经济衰退以来，市场无法自我调节以惠及多数人，需要亲工人的政府干预。

• [jt-hill] 提到了“The Sort”概念，指出在较差的工作中所需的软技能在其他角色中能获得更好的回报，社会在有效分配人力资源方面做得更好。

• [I_Nidhi] 认为如果员工在面试中表现出色并获得了工作，他们就应该能够胜任。她强调问题的根源往往在于角色或工作的清晰度，而非员工的动机。

• [bluedevilzn] 反驳了支付更多费用就能获得更好服务的观点，分享了自己以高价雇佣本地工人但仍遭遇劣质服务的经历。

• [wnolens] 指出北美人重视廉价商品和服务，往往不关心背后的生产过程。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于工作质量低下的原因以及解决方案。一部分人认为是经济模式和低薪导致工人无法提供优质服务，另一部分人则强调态度和文化差异对工作表现的影响。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是政府和市场在解决这些问题中的角色，部分评论者呼吁政府干预，而其他人则认为市场自我调节是解决方案。
• 不同经济模式（如零工经济与传统全职工作）对工人生活和职业发展的影响也被广泛讨论。

data.title: Building Gearbox Dynamometer
data.author: nill0
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者Mateo Peña Doll自制了一个齿轮箱测功机（dynamometer），用于测试他设计和制造的船用变速箱。这些变速箱主要用于电动水翼船的较低单元齿轮箱。由于外包测试成本高昂（每小时100美元以上），作者决定自制一个AC测功机，以进行长达1000小时的耐久性测试。

该测功机包括8020铝框架、电机控制器调校、应变片校准等，并集成了自定义扭矩测量、水冷却、CAN总线以及基于Python的仪表板。测功机通过输入电机提供动力，再生电机输出动力，系统效率约为70%。它能连续处理30kW功率，峰值达50kW。

传感器测量包括扭矩、速度、温度、内部齿轮箱压力等数据，所有数据通过Arduino采集，并使用MongoDB进行存储和分析，通过Python仪表板实时监控。作者的自制方案有效降低了成本，并提供了丰富的数据支持变速箱测试。

• [nraynaud] 通过年轻时的经历，讲述了在1000HP测功机上因速度传感器皮带断裂导致的严重设备损坏事件，强调了高功率测试中的潜在危险和设备故障带来的严重后果。
