data.title: Dijkstra On the foolishness of "natural language programming"
data.author: nimbleplum40
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了使用自然语言进行编程的不可行性。作者认为，从计算历史看，编程需要精确的形式化符号，尽管早期有人希望机器能自动纠正明显错误。尽管高层次编程语言减少了一些错误，但机器仍会忠实执行无意义的指令。有人建议用自然语言编程以简化操作，但这会增加机器的复杂性，且未必简化人类的工作。数学史表明，形式化符号的使用推动了科学进步，而非自然语言。自然语言容易产生不易察觉的错误，而形式化符号则能有效避免无意义操作。因此，使用正式符号应被视为一种便利，而非负担。若一开始就用自然语言编程，计算机科学可能仍会重蹈覆辙，依赖复杂而无效的表达。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自然语言与编程语言在软件开发中的适用性及优缺点

不同观点：
• [01100011] 认为将代码转换回自然语言可能会丢失细节，无法还原程序的复杂性和精确性。自然语言难以管理高复杂度和精确性的项目，因此法律文件等使用复杂语言是为了避免歧义和确保精确。
• [haolez] 引用Hal Abelson的话，强调计算机科学的核心是程序性认识论，计算提供了一种从命令式角度处理知识结构的框架，而数学则是从陈述式角度处理知识。自然语言和编程语言在表达方式上有根本区别。
• [l0new0lf-G] 支持[01100011]的观点，认为自然语言有其固有的局限性，可能会导致过于抽象或过于具体，难以保持适当的细节，且解释清楚往往比直接写代码更耗时。
• [Someone] 提出一种极端观点，认为可以通过自然语言直接运行提示来生成和操作程序，如通过详细的自然语言描述来控制图形系统、文件系统等。这种方法目前尚未成熟，但未来可能会有所发展。
• [sotix] 认为使用LLM进行编程像是半智能的猜测游戏，而Rust编译器通过指出错误和建议修复更能帮助开发者，因此更倾向于传统的编译器和编程语言的演进。
• [llsf] 强调自然语言不适合用来传达规则和指令，举例说明即使是法律条文也会因语言的模糊性而产生争议，编程需要精确的表达。
• [misja111] 认为自然语言到形式语言的转换不可避免，尤其是在商业环境中，新功能的想法通常由非技术人员提出，需要经过翻译才能实现。
• [indigoabstract] 将自然语言编程比作游戏设计文档，认为虽然在初期有帮助，但最终实现会成为主要参考，而文档往往会被抛弃。
• [weeeee2] 讨论自然语言对人类和计算机的“自然”性问题，认为AI若不受限于人类语言可能会发明更适合其架构的语言，因此存在人与AI之间的本质不匹配。
• [truculent] 认为任何足够高级的编程方法最终都会看起来更像编程语言，而不是自然语言。如果不想编程，也需要通过教育来指导智能系统。
• [centra_minded] 指出当代编程已经远离严格的符号主义，大多数程序员使用高层次的抽象和框架，而不完全理解其内部工作原理。LLM编程可能进一步加剧这种分离。
• [octacat] 认为自然语言适合描述复杂系统的技术需求和高层设计，但不适合具体的代码实现。编程语言在局部范围内提供了无歧义的表达，但在全局范围内可能失效。
• [hamstergene] 通过多个历史上的失败案例（如流图、弱类型、约束布局等）说明某些看似简单的想法往往在实践中失败，建议软件工程应建立一个“不可行想法的殿堂”以警示新人。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于自然语言是否适合用于编程及描述复杂系统。一方认为自然语言过于模糊且难以管理复杂性，另一方则认为在特定情况下可以通过AI的帮助实现自然语言编程。
• 对LLM在编程中的角色存在争议，一些人认为其帮助有限且可能导致不精确，另一些人则看好其未来发展潜力。
• 自然语言与编程语言的本质区别和适用场景是讨论的核心，不同观点强调了各自的优缺点及潜在应用场景。

43564386.article_content:
EWD 667
On the foolishness of "natural language programming"
.
Since the early days of automatic computing we have had people that have felt it as a shortcoming that programming required the care and accuracy that is characteristic for the use of any formal symbolism. They blamed the mechanical slave for its strict obedience with which it carried out its given instructions, even if a moment's thought would have revealed that those instructions contained an obvious mistake. "But a moment is a long time, and thought is a painful process." (A.E.Houseman). They eagerly hoped and waited for more sensible machinery that would refuse to embark on such nonsensical activities as a trivial clerical error evoked at the time.
Machine code, with its absence of almost any form of redundancy, was soon identified as a needlessly risky interface between man and machine. Partly in response to this recognition so-called "high-level programming languages" were developed, and, as time went by, we learned to a certain extent how to enhance the protection against silly mistakes. It was a significant improvement that now many a silly mistake did result in an error message instead of in an erroneous answer. (And even this improvement wasn't universally appreciated: some people found error messages they couldn't ignore more annoying than wrong results, and, when judging the relative merits of programming languages, some still seem to equate "the ease of programming" with the ease of making undetected mistakes.) The (abstract) machine corresponding to a programming language remained, however, a faithful slave, i.e. the nonsensible automaton perfectly capable of carrying out nonsensical instructions. Programming remained the use of a formal symbolism and, as such, continued to require the care and accuracy required before.
In order to make machines significantly easier to use, it has been proposed (to try) to design machines that we could instruct in our native tongues. this would, admittedly, make the machines much more complicated, but, it was argued, by letting the machine carry a larger share of the burden, life would become easier for us. It sounds sensible provided you blame the obligation to use a formal symbolism as the source of your difficulties. But is the argument valid? I doubt.
We know in the meantime that the choice of an interface is not just a division of (a fixed amount of) labour, because the work involved in co-operating and communicating across the interface has to be added. We know in the meantime —from sobering experience, I may add— that a change of interface can easily increase at both sides of the fence the amount of work to be done (even drastically so). Hence the increased preference for what are now called "narrow interfaces". Therefore, although changing to communication between machine and man conducted in the latter's native tongue would greatly increase the machine's burden, we have to challenge the assumption that this would simplify man's life.
A short look at the history of mathematics shows how justified this challenge is. Greek mathematics got stuck because it remained a verbal, pictorial activity, Moslem "algebra", after a timid attempt at symbolism, died when it returned to the rhetoric style, and the modern civilized world could only emerge —for better or for worse— when Western Europe could free itself from the fetters of medieval scholasticism —a vain attempt at verbal precision!— thanks to the carefully, or at least consciously designed formal symbolisms that we owe to people like Vieta, Descartes, Leibniz, and (later) Boole.
The virtue of formal texts is that their manipulations, in order to be legitimate, need to satisfy only a few simple rules; they are, when you come to think of it, an amazingly effective tool for ruling out all sorts of nonsense that, when we use our native tongues, are almost impossible to avoid.
Instead of regarding the obligation to use formal symbols as a burden, we should regard the convenience of using them as a privilege: thanks to them, school children can learn to do what in earlier days only genius could achieve. (This was evidently not understood by the author that wrote —in 1977— in the preface of a technical report that "even the standard symbols used for logical connectives have been avoided for the sake of clarity". The occurrence of that sentence suggests that the author's misunderstanding is not confined to him alone.) When all is said and told, the "naturalness" with which we use our native tongues boils down to the ease with which we can use them for making statements the nonsense of which is not obvious.
It may be illuminating to try to imagine what would have happened if, right from the start our native tongue would have been the only vehicle for the input into and the output from our information processing equipment. data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种使用单一CSS自定义属性生成模糊图像占位符（LQIP）的技术，无需复杂标记或JavaScript。通过设置如``的属性值，即可显示非常模糊的占位图。这种方法的优势在于其简便和非侵入性，避免了使用额外包装元素或长数据字符串。 文章还比较了其他LQIP方法，如低分辨率WebP、JPEG、SVG优化（SQIP）、BlurHash等。其中，BlurHash通过短base-83字符串压缩图像数据，但需要JavaScript解码。而作者提出的纯CSS方案通过将图像数据编码为单个整数实现，利用位打包技术在20位整数内存储图像信息（一个基础颜色和六个亮度分量），实现极简的LQIP。 尽管这种CSS方法生成的占位图非常模糊，但其优点在于简洁和避免了标记膨胀。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CSS中的创新用法及其在LQIP（Low-Quality Image Placeholders）实现中的性能和效果

不同观点：
• esprehn赞赏使用CSS的巧妙方法，但建议避免在样式属性上使用attr选择器，如[style*="--lqip:"]，因为这可能导致性能问题。他提议使用单独的布尔属性或类来避免性能瓶颈，并提供了相关技术文档支持其观点。
• WorldMaker指出，在滑块探索LQIP空间时，如果将基础颜色编码在高比特而不是低比特，可以减少闪烁。这是一个关于视觉效果的审美建议。
• matthberg对独立设置每个部分的亮度值（L值）提出疑问，并建议从基础颜色的L值中削减两位以优化编码。他还提出使用OKLab颜色空间进行径向渐变的中心调整，以获得更美观的视觉效果。
• mubou对使用CSS实现二进制编码算法表示印象深刻，并提出是否可以将其用于生成独特的几何图案，如通用头像。
• mattdesl赞赏该项目，并建议尝试在OKLab颜色空间中提取主色以改进颜色窃取算法。他还提到使用遗传算法寻找理想匹配的可能性，并指出在Safari浏览器中的兼容性问题。
• emsixteen对CSS实现纯客户端占位图的效果表示困惑，质疑是否需要先下载图像再进行处理。这是一个关于技术实现原理的疑问。
• chmod775认为该页面在手机上的性能较差，导致滚动时卡顿。这是一个关于性能问题的反馈。
• throwaway2016a赞赏该解决方案，认为相比纯色占位符效果更好，并指出在特定图像上的技术局限性。
• Cieric提醒注意Dark Reader插件对最终颜色的影响，导致颜色不匹配的问题。这是一个关于浏览器插件兼容性的反馈。
• bufferoverflow认为应使用WebP v2来实现此类效果，并提供了一个具体工具和压缩效果对比。这是一个关于技术选型的建议。
• ssttoo提到另一种简单的CSS解决方案，即使用渐变背景，并提供了一个工具链接。这是另一种实现方式的示例。
• duffyjp分享了自己以前使用服务器端生成小图像并进行base64编码的实验经验，并认为该CSS解决方案在视觉效果上更好。
• layer8幽默地提到自己最初误读了文章标题，这是一个轻松的插曲。
• biker142541对该CSS方法的效果表示赞赏，并计划尝试使用该方法来改进自己的项目。
• bmandale分享了自己尝试四色方法的链接，提供了一个具体实现的示例。

补充讨论：
• 关于性能问题的讨论主要集中在esprehn的技术建议和chmod775的实际性能反馈。
• 关于视觉效果和实现原理的讨论主要集中在WorldMaker、matthberg和mattdesl的建议和疑问。
• 关于技术选型和兼容性的讨论主要集中在mattdesl、Cieric和bufferoverflow的反馈。

43523220.article_content: Here’s a CSS technique that produces blurry image placeholders (LQIPs) without cluttering up your markup — Only a single custom property needed! The custom property above gives you this image: Try changing the property’s value (WARNING: FLASHING) Granted, it’s a very blurry placeholder especially in contrast to other leading solutions. But the point is that it’s minimal and non-invasive! No need for wrapper elements or attributes with long strings of data, or JavaScript at all. Note for RSS readers / ‘Reader’ mode clients: This post makes heavy use of CSS-based images. Your client may not support it. Example images Toggle images Check out the LQIP gallery for examples! Survey of LQIP approaches There have been many different techniques to implement LQIPs (low quality image placeholders), such as a very low resolution WebP or JPEG ( beheaded JPEGs even), optimised SVG shape placements ( SQIP ), and directly applying a discrete cosine transform ( BlurHash ). Don’t forget good old progressive JPEGs and interlaced PNGs! Canva and Pinterest use solid colour placeholders. At the other end of the spectrum, we have low tech solutions such as a simple solid fill of the image’s average colour. Pure inline CSS solutions have the advantage rendering immediately — even a background-image: url(…a data URL) would be fine! Gradify generates linear-gradients that very roughly approximate the full image. The big disadvantage of pure CSS approaches is that you typically litter your markup with lengthy inline styles or obnoxious data URLs. My handcoded site with no build step would be extra incompatible with this approach! BlurHash is a solution that minimises markup by compressing image data into a short base-83 string , but decoding and rendering that data requires additional JS… BlurHash example Is it possible to decode a blur hash in CSS instead? Decoding in pure CSS Unlike BlurHash, we can’t use a string encoding because there are very few if any string manipulation functions in CSS (2025), so strings are out. In the end, I came up with my own hash / encoding, and the integer type was the best vessel for it. The usual way to encode stuff in a single integer is by bit packing , where you pack multiple numbers in an integer as bits. Amazingly, we can unpack them in pure CSS! To unpack bits, all you need is bit shifting and bit masking. Bit shifting can be done by division and floor operations — calc(x / y) and round(down,n) — and bit masking via the modulo function mod(a,b) . * { /* Example packed int: */ /* 0b11_00_001_101 */ --packed-int: 781; --bits-9-10: mod(round(down, calc(var(--packed-int) / 256)), 4); /* 3 */ --bits-7-8: mod(round(down, calc(var(--packed-int) / 64)), 4); /* 0 */ --bits-4-6: mod(round(down, calc(var(--packed-int) / 8)), 8); /* 1 */ --bits-0-3: mod(var(--packed-int), 8); /* 5 */ } Of course, we could also use pow(2,n) instead of hardcoded powers of two. So, a single CSS integer value was going to be the encoding of the “hash” of my CSS-only blobhash (that’s what I’m calling it now). But how much information can we pack in a single CSS int? Side quest: Limits of CSS values The spec doesn’t say anything about the allowed range for int values, leaving the fate of my shenanigans to browser vendors. From my experiments, apparently you can only use integers from -999,999 up to 999,999 in custom properties before you lose precision. Just beyond that limit, we start getting values rounded to tens — 1,234,56 7 becomes 1,234,56 0 . Which is weird (precision is counted in decimal places!?), but I bet it’s due to historical, Internet Explorer-esque reasons. Anyway, within the range of [-999999, 999999] there are 1,999,999 values. This meant that with a single integer hash, almost two million LQIP configurations could be described. To make calculation easier, I reduced it to the nearest power of two down which is 2 20 . 2 20 = 1,048,576 < 1,999,999 < 2,097,152 = 2 21 In short, I had 20 bits of information to encode the CSS-based LQIP hash. Why is it called a “hash”? Because it’s a mapping from an any-size data to a fixed-size value. In this case, there are an infinite number of images of arbitrary sizes, but only 1,999,999 possible hash values. The Scheme With only 20 bits, the LQIP image must be a very simplified version of the full image. I ended up with this scheme: a single base colour + 6 brightness components, to be overlaid on top of the base colour in a 3×2 grid. A rather extreme version of chroma subsampling . data.title: Hacking the call records of millions of Americans
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary: 文章披露了Verizon移动服务中的一个安全漏洞，该漏洞允许任何人通过Verizon Call Filter iOS应用查询其他用户的通话记录，包括来电号码和时间戳，而无需设备权限或密码。这一漏洞源于服务器未验证请求中的电话号码是否与登录用户匹配，攻击者只需修改请求中的电话号码，即可获取其他用户的通话历史。这种数据泄露对普通用户是隐私侵犯，对记者、执法人员、公众人物和家暴受害者等可能构成安全威胁。通过分析通话元数据，攻击者可以重建目标的日常活动、识别频繁联系人、推断个人关系，甚至追踪其物理行踪。技术上，问题出现在未验证电话号码的API端点，导致大规模用户信息暴露。Verizon已修复此问题，但该事件凸显了电信数据保护的脆弱性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Verizon安全漏洞及其影响

不同观点：
• twalkz：对Verizon未验证手机号码与用户身份绑定表示担忧，认为这是严重的疏忽，并质疑公司是否应公开该漏洞是否曾被滥用。
• dotty-：指出Verizon Call Filter应用使用了一个看似内部的域名，暗示其安全性可能不足。
• devmtk：对Verizon这样的大公司出现这种问题感到惊讶，认为需要有人对安全问题负责，并担心是否有其他泄露问题。
• adxl：质疑渗透测试和安全负责人的角色，认为这是明显的安全漏洞，好在及时修复。
• chatmasta：认为通话记录早已广泛存在于账单和多个系统中，可能已经泄露，强调技术供应商控制脆弱服务器的问题。
• MPSFounder：希望Verizon为此支付高额漏洞赏金，否则认为公司不会吸取教训，并批评管理层的态度。
• vivzkestrel：对如何发现此类漏洞感到好奇，询问是否需要全职进行这种研究，以及如何找到未被发现的问题。
• grg0：质疑为何此事件未成为重大新闻，认为政府和媒体对企业问题的忽视与政治利益有关。
• coolThingsFirst：对如何拦截移动应用的API调用表示好奇。
• metalman：认为此类问题不应称为“黑客攻击”，批评电话记录访问缺乏正式程序，并质疑对隐私权的侵犯。

补充讨论：
• 对Verizon安全漏洞的技术细节和潜在影响的关注。
• 对公司责任和漏洞披露透明度的讨论。
• 对安全漏洞发现过程和伦理黑客工作方式的好奇。
• 对企业与政府关系及媒体报道偏向的政治评论。
• 对电话记录隐私和安全性的广泛担忧。

43558550.article_content:
Hacking the Call Records of Millions of Americans
Imagine if anyone could punch in a phone number from the largest U.S. cell carrier and instantly retrieve a list of its recent incoming calls—complete with timestamps—without compromising the device, guessing a password, or alerting the user.
Now imagine that number belongs to a journalist, a police officer, a politician, or someone fleeing an abuser.
This capability wasn’t a hypothetical.
I recently identified a security vulnerability in the
Verizon Call Filter iOS app
which made it possible for an attacker to leak call history logs of Verizon Wireless customers.
Call logs can be quite valuable, especially for nation states, as recently noted in coverage of the Salt Typhoon breach of telecom networks:
https://www.nytimes.com/2024/10/25/us/politics/trump-vance-hack.html
Given that this data is of such value, you’d expect that both how it’s accessed, and who is given access would be closely guarded. However, as I found, this may not be the case.
High level overview:
In order to display your recent history of received calls in the Verizon Call Filter app, a network request is made to a server. That request contains various details such as your phone number and the requested time period for call records. The server then responds with a list of calls and timestamps for each.
So surely the server validated that the phone number being requested was tied to the signed in user? Right? Right?? Well…no. It was possible to modify the phone number being sent, and then receive data back for Verizon numbers not associated with the signed in user.
In short, anyone could lookup data for anyone.
This is of course a privacy concern for all. But for some this could also represent a safety concern.
Consider scenarios involving survivors of domestic abuse, law enforcement officers, or public figures—individuals who rely on the confidentiality of their communication patterns. Having their incoming call logs exposed is not just invasive; it’s dangerous.
Call metadata might seem harmless, but in the wrong hands, it becomes a powerful surveillance tool. With unrestricted access to another user’s call history, an attacker could reconstruct daily routines, identify frequent contacts, and infer personal relationships.
Timestamps can be cross-referenced with social media or public sightings to map physical movements. Repeated numbers expose private or burner lines, compromising whistleblowers, journalists, or abuse survivors.
This wasn’t just a data leak. It was a real-time surveillance mechanism waiting to be abused.
Technical details:
The Verizon Call Filter app uses the endpoint
https://clr-aqx.cequintvzwecid.com/clr/callLogRetrieval
to lookup call history for the authenticated user and display it in the app.
This endpoint requires a JWT (JSON Web Token) in the Authorization header using the Bearer scheme and uses an
X-Ceq-MDN
header to specify a cell phone number to retrieve call history logs for.
A JWT has three parts: header, payload, and signature. It’s often used for authentication and authorization in web apps.
The payload in this case looked like:
{
"sub"
:
"SIGNED_IN_USER_PHONE_NUMBER_HERE"
,
"iat"
:
"1740253712"
,
"iss"
:
"df88f1ed1dfd9a903e4c8dca7f00089e134c6c4e0a566cd565147ba1dadf78a6"
,
"secret"
:
"REDACTED"
,
"alg"
:
"ECDSA-256"
,
"exp"
:
"1740255512"
}
sub
stands for subject — it identifies who the token is about (usually the user ID). In this case that is a phone number of the signed in user.
What should have been happening, and did seem to take place on other endpoints for additional app functionality, is that the server would compare the phone number specified in the request to the user identifier (sub) in the JWT, to ensure that the user requesting the information should have access to it.
However, the
/clr/callLogRetrieval
endpoint was not validating that the phone number specified in the
X-Ceq-MDN
header matches the
sub
in the JWT payload, meaning it was possible to lookup call history logs for any phone number within the application by passing the desired phone number in the value of that header.
Example Vulnerable Request:
The issue I discovered impacted at least those who have the Verizon Call Filter service enabled (I did not test a number which had it disabled; I can’t rule out whether or not all Verizon numbers could have been impacted).
Based on
https://www.verizon.com/support/call-filter-faqs/
and
https://www.verizon.com/about/news/verizon-helps-customers-avoid-15-billion-robocalls
I believe this service may be on by default for many/all Verizon Wireless customers, so in either case, it does seem this issue impacted either nearly all, or all customers.
While this endpoint
only
returned received calls for the specified phone number, I don’t believe that to be a major limitation on impact. For one, that’s still an immense amount of information. But also, for a targeted individual, this could stretch into a partial picture of outgoing calls as well, provided

主要讨论点：美国政治与商业腐败，尤其是特朗普政府与苹果公司的关系，以及大科技公司与政治权力的互动。

不同观点：
• **[throw4847285]** 引用历史和理论分析，指出社会在统治者圈子缩小的同时得到“拯救”，并将任何改革要求都打上“社会主义”标签。该评论强调了政治秩序与财产、宗教等名义下的暴力和镇压。

• **[jp57]** 对金融时报（FT）使用“group”指代苹果公司感到困惑，以为是指更大的硅谷公司群体，而非单独的苹果公司。

• **[arunabha]** 指出有选民因相信“拜登/克林顿/奥巴马/索罗斯阴谋集团”导致美国腐败而投票支持现任政府，具有讽刺意味。

• **[bigyabai]** 认为欧盟不会撤回对苹果的诉讼，导致苹果产品在消费者法规上出现分化，并质疑美国人对苹果的信任是否会受到影响。

• **[rchaud]** 提到苹果CEO蒂姆·库克在2025年向特朗普就职典礼捐赠100万美元，认为这是为了团结，但可能有其他动机。

• **[jimnotgym]** 假设特朗普政权结束，可能会对苹果不利。

• **[nova22033]** 指出Morgan Lewis律师事务所为埃隆·马斯克和亚马逊处理劳资纠纷，认为这是理所当然的。

• **[croes]** 质疑普通特朗普支持者何时会意识到特朗普并不为他们工作，暗指特朗普“排干华盛顿沼泽”的承诺落空。

• **[throwaway5752]** 谴责2025年美国的政治腐败，认为这将阻碍创新，并指出Hacker News和YCombinator应对此采取行动。

• **[9283409232]** 对特朗普政府没有对苹果采取报复行动感到意外，猜测特朗普是否在帮助苹果以期回报。

• **[guerrilla]** 认为美国的政治腐败长期存在，但如今变得如此明目张胆，以至于令人震惊，并将其比作某些落后的国家。

• **[bananapub]** 强调了监管机构被大公司完全控制的现状，指出特朗普提名代表苹果的律师担任NLRB总法律顾问，显示出公司对国家权力的影响。

• **[duxup]** 觉得本届政府的每个任命似乎都有腐败动机。

• 评论中多次提到苹果与特朗普政府的关系，尤其是库克的捐赠行为和监管案件的处理，显示出大科技公司与政治权力的复杂互动。
• 政治腐败和公司对国家权力的影响是讨论的核心，评论者对这种现象普遍持批评态度。
• 争议的焦点在于特朗普政府是否在利用职权为大公司谋利，以及这种行为对社会和创新的潜在影响。

主要讨论点：中美在电动汽车（EV）市场的竞争与进展

不同观点：
• kristopolous 引用Aspen Aerogels的CFO Ricardo C. Rodriguez的观点，指出中国在电动汽车市场上的渗透率已经达到50%，而北美和欧洲仅在10%到15%之间徘徊。他认为，在这种背景下，继续与中国进行“贸易战”如同自残，因为中国在电动汽车领域已经取得显著进展，而西方进展缓慢。

• 01HNNWZ0MV43FF 批评美国汽车行业甚至无法推出一款类似于丰田普锐斯的国产电动汽车，暗示美国在电动汽车制造上的落后，并认为这是一个明显的失败。

• bpodgursky 指出中国并没有在电动汽车领域受到抵制，并预言中国企业比亚迪（BYD）将会在全球市场取得主导地位，认为西方对中国的限制措施是自损行为。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于中美在电动汽车市场中的竞争态势。一方认为中国已经大幅领先，而西方国家的进展缓慢；另一方则批评美国在制造电动汽车方面的失败，并认为中国企业将主导全球市场。

• 评论中还提到了“贸易战”和市场竞争的策略问题，有观点认为继续对抗中国可能会导致自损，特别是在中国已经取得显著市场渗透的情况下。

• 比亚迪（BYD）被特别提到作为中国电动汽车企业的代表，评论者认为其有可能在全球范围内取得成功，进一步加剧了西方国家在电动汽车市场竞争中的焦虑。

data.article_summary: The New Stack邀请软件工程领导者和有抱负的开发者加入他们的社区，通过电子邮件获取最新的软件开发新闻和独家内容。如果之前退订过，需要重新订阅。他们承诺不会将用户信息出售或分享给第三方。新用户需填写个人信息（如姓名、公司、国家等）和职业信息（如职位、角色、公司规模等），以确保提供相关内容。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NVIDIA CuTile、Triton、GPU与CPU编程模型、跨平台开发以及Python在GPU计算中的角色。

不同观点：
• **ashvardanian**：认为CuTile是Triton的后继者，并对TileIR和CuPy的SIMT编程模型表示赞赏。然而，他指出NVIDIA在CPU方面的支持不足，尤其是Grace CPU，并认为目前缺少跨CPU和GPU的通用抽象，这给并行算法开发带来了困难。他还提到Modular团队在多平台开发上的努力，并希望Mojo语言能填补CPU-GPU的鸿沟。

• **diggan**：作为一个非GPU程序员，他发现高层次的API（如CuTile）在基本操作上使用简单，且性能显著优于CPU。他认为CUDA编程如果没有这样的高层次工具会非常繁琐。

• **btown**：对NVIDIA在GTC 2025上展示的全栈方法表示赞赏，特别是新的Tile IR和cuTile库。然而，他也指出新的IR可能会扩大与其它平台（如ZLUDA和AMD工具）的差距。

• **aixpert**：感谢Pytorch在NVIDIA专用工具之前就获得了广泛应用，使得开发者不必局限于NVIDIA的特定工具。他希望新的平台能将GPU计算的概念扩展到更多领域，比如游戏。

• **gymbeaux**：认为这是巨大的进步，尤其是对那些不愿学习C++的开发者而言。他强调Python直接访问GPU的效率影响，并指出这对能源消耗的积极意义。

• **odo1242**：认为CuPy和Numba已经提供了类似的功能，但官方支持仍然是一个亮点。

• **the__alchemist**：希望看到Rust支持，因为目前需要手动序列化数据结构，非常不便。

• **ryao**：希望看到一个真正的C变体CUDA，而不是扩展C++的CUDA C。

• **math_dandy**：想了解NVIDIA的JIT编译器与JAX的JIT编译器之间的关系和区别。

• **matt3210**：建议为GPU找一个新的名称，因为GPU的原始用途已经过时。

• **lunarboy**：认为AMD可以创建类似的Python API来针对其硬件，从而降低Nvidia GPU的粘性。

• **jmward01**：认为Python的广泛采用会带来更多的快速试验和目标实现，这对开发者是好事。

• **chrisrodrigue**：认为Python正在成为编程语言的通用语，其在FOSS复兴中的地位不可动摇，并期待性能的持续提升。

• **CapsAdmin**：分享了使用LuaJIT和CUDA进行llama 3推理的经验，指出API的状态性问题和调试困难。

• **steelbrain**：提到tinygrad项目，一个反向工程的Python-only GPU API，支持CUDA和AMD ROCm，提供了其它运行时的选择。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：NVIDIA在CPU和GPU之间缺乏通用抽象，给并行算法开发带来了困难。
• 重要论据：Python的高层次API简化了GPU编程，降低了学习曲线和开发难度。
• 其它讨论：开发者对Rust支持的期待、JIT编译器的比较、以及Python在GPU计算中的角色增强。

• **btown**：对NVIDIA在GTC 2025上展示的全栈方法表示赞赏，特别是新的Tile IR和cuTile库。然而，他也指出新的IR可能会扩大与其它平台（如ZLUDA和AMD工具）的差距。

• **aixpert**：感谢Pytorch在NVIDIA专用工具之前就获得了广泛应用，使得开发者不必局限于NVIDIA的特定工具。他希望新的平台能将GPU计算的概念扩展到更多领域，比如游戏。

• **gymbeaux**：认为这是巨大的进步，尤其是对那些不愿学习C++的开发者而言。他强调Python直接访问GPU的效率影响，并指出这对能源消耗的积极意义。

• **odo1242**：认为CuPy和Numba已经提供了类似的功能，但官方支持仍然是一个亮点。

• **the__alchemist**：希望看到Rust支持，因为目前需要手动序列化数据结构，非常不便。

• **ryao**：希望看到一个真正的C变体CUDA，而不是扩展C++的CUDA C。

• **math_dandy**：想了解NVIDIA的JIT编译器与JAX的JIT编译器之间的关系和区别。

• **matt3210**：建议为GPU找一个新的名称，因为GPU的原始用途已经过时。

• **lunarboy**：认为AMD可以创建类似的Python API来针对其硬件，从而降低Nvidia GPU的粘性。

• **jmward01**：认为Python的广泛采用会带来更多的快速试验和目标实现，这对开发者是好事。

• **chrisrodrigue**：认为Python正在成为编程语言的通用语，其在FOSS复兴中的地位不可动摇，并期待性能的持续提升。

• **CapsAdmin**：分享了使用LuaJIT和CUDA进行llama 3推理的经验，指出API的状态性问题和调试困难。

• **steelbrain**：提到tinygrad项目，一个反向工程的Python-only GPU API，支持CUDA和AMD ROCm，提供了其它运行时的选择。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：NVIDIA在CPU和GPU之间缺乏通用抽象，给并行算法开发带来了困难。
• 重要论据：Python的高层次API简化了GPU编程，降低了学习曲线和开发难度。
• 其它讨论：开发者对Rust支持的期待、JIT编译器的比较、以及Python在GPU计算中的角色增强。

主要讨论点：是否存在一个有效的政治倾向测验生成工具（political compass generator）

不同观点：
• 观点一：认为存在有效的政治倾向测验工具。支持者认为像"Political Compass"这样的工具通过多维度的问题测试，可以较为准确地反映一个人的政治倾向，包括经济和社会的左右立场。这些工具常被用作自我反思或教育用途，帮助人们了解自己的政治定位。

• 观点二：质疑政治倾向测验工具的准确性和科学性。反对者指出，这类工具可能存在问题设计上的偏见或不够全面，导致结果不一定准确。他们认为政治倾向是一个复杂的、多维度的概念，简单的在线测试难以全面捕捉。此外，有人认为这些问题往往过于宽泛或模糊，容易导致误解或误导。

• 观点三：认为政治倾向测验工具只是娱乐性质。一些评论者认为这些工具主要用于娱乐，结果不必太过认真对待。他们指出，用户可能会因为个人偏见或情绪化回答而得到不准确的结果，因此工具的实际参考价值有限。

补充讨论：
• 关于工具的多维度性：有讨论提到一些工具仅关注经济和社会的左右，而忽略了其他重要的政治维度，如环境政策、外交政策等，这可能限制其全面性。

• 争议焦点：主要争议在于这些工具的准确性和科学性，以及它们是否能够真实反映一个人的政治倾向。部分用户分享了彼此使用不同工具得到不一致结果的经历，进一步质疑其可靠性。

• 使用场景：一些支持者提到这些工具在教育和讨论中的价值，特别是在引导政治讨论和帮助人们理解不同政治立场方面。反对者则认为，这些工具在这些场景中的应用可能导致误导性的结论或刻板印象。

data.title: Why does Britain feel so poor?
data.author: prawn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国社会和经济的“贫穷感”及其原因

不同观点：
• [IndianITGuy] 认为财富并没有消失，而是从公共领域撤出并隐藏在私人领域中。富人将大量资金投入私人住宅和个人享受，而忽视公共基础设施的投资，导致公共空间破败，给人一种“英国变穷了”的感觉。
• [gchadwick] 强调地方政府在维护公共设施（如道路、儿童游乐设施、公共厕所等）方面的无能为力和资金短缺，指出社会关怀和特殊教育需求（SEND）成本的急剧上升是导致地方财政困难的主要原因。
• [gghhzzgghhzz] 批评公共服务和基础设施的私有化和外包，认为这些系统被金融化，导致成本增加且效率低下，同时政治和公共叙事被用来推动更多私有化。
• [Danieru] 认为问题不在于税收不足，而在于资金使用不当，批评政府的无效管理和追逐新闻头条的做法，并提到英国需要找到不妥协的解决方案。
• [p0d] 对所见贫富差距感到困惑，表示在不同地区（如贝尔法斯特和一些贫困地区）的经历让他对英国的贫穷感有不同看法。
• [docdeek] 强调规划和审批流程的复杂性，指出繁琐的审批程序是导致高开发成本和项目延误的原因。
• [proaralyst] 认为英国的规划系统（如《城乡规划法》）是导致高开发成本和项目困难的主要原因，并与其他国家的更简化的规划系统进行对比。
• [masfuerte] 批评HS2项目中的浪费和不当决策，认为某些昂贵的项目设计是为了最大化利润而不是为了有效的解决方案。
• [petercooper] 将英国比作一个靠积累财富和声望生活的退休者，指出英国在生产力和收入方面落后。
• [jwhiles] 认为伦敦某些地区不建设高密度住房是导致住房短缺和经济问题的原因。
• [samiv] 和 [jmathai] 提到Gary's Economics的视频，认为主流经济学家未能预测或改善经济，并讨论财富不平等和财富零和游戏的观点。
• [potato3732842] 认为繁琐的检查和平衡系统已经变得过于庞大，成为问题的一部分，而不是解决方案。
• [WalterBright] 引用C. Northcote Parkinson的观点，认为20世纪初官僚国家的兴起和税收的增加是英国衰退的开始。
• [tremon] 认为过去20年的政策过于集中在伦敦，忽视了其他地区的发展，导致这些地区在国家政策下挣扎，同时争夺有限的资金。

补充讨论：
• 公共投资与私人投资的失衡：许多人指出，私人财富的增加并未转化为公共福利的提升，而是更多地投入私人享受和奢侈品。
• 地方政府的无能为力：地方政府在面对社会关怀和SEND成本上升时缺乏资金和控制权，导致公共设施和服务质量下降。
• 规划和审批的复杂性：繁琐的审批程序和高昂的开发成本被认为是导致基础设施项目延误和失败的原因。
• 财富不平等和金融化：讨论涉及财富不平等的加剧和金融系统对经济的影响，认为新财富的创造不足以弥补现有财富分配的不平衡。
• 政策集中于伦敦：批评政府政策过于集中在伦敦，忽视其他地区的发展需求，导致全国范围内的经济不平衡。

data.title: An AlphaStation's SROM
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了作者对一台90年代的AlphaStation 500工作站的修复过程，特别是其启动机制和SROM（串行ROM）的解析。AlphaStation 500不同于常见的PC，它没有传统的BIOS，而是通过SROM和CPU内部逻辑进行启动。SROM包含八个多路复用的映像，通过主板上的跳线选择其中一个进行启动。作者试图分析SROM内容以解决机器的RAM问题，并使用闪存编程器读取和分解SROM数据。尽管找到了SROM的源码参考，但尚未确定具体的"迷你控制台"输出位置。作者提供了分解SROM的Python代码，并分享了读取的SROM二进制文件以供进一步分析。

Background
I have a thing for
weird
90's
RISC workstations running UNIX. So when Rob said "Hey, I have an AlphaStation in the boot of my car ..." obviously it came home with me.
Unfortunately the AlphaStation is dead. The PSU runs (and stays running, unless the case are disconnected in which case it immediately stops running). The voltages look fine. But the two PCI cards in the machine (a 32-bit Matrox Millenium G200 graphics card and a 64-bit LSI Logic SCSI card) are both dead - neither is detected when inserted into my Pentium 3 PC. And half of the RAM in the first DIMM slot gets very hot. So, I suspect something catastrophic has happened somewhere in its lifetime. But, at least I got a 18GB 1.6" SCSI Hard Drive out of it, and a working (ish) 12x SCSI CD-ROM.
The AlphaStation 500
This isn't a post about the AlphaStation 500. I'll save that for when (if) I get it working. This is a post about how an AlphaStation 500 boots. But here it is.
The AlphaStation 500 is a workstation from Digital, circa 1996. Mine is a 500 MHz model and has an Alpha 21164A processor (aka EV56). And the way it boots is
weird
.
On your common-or-garden PC, there has always been some kind of ROM chip. It holds a piece of firmware known as the BIOS. This ROM chip is available at a well-known location in the processor's address space (remembering that any PC processor boots up in 16-bit, 8088 compatible mode, with a 1 MiB address space, just like an IBM PC 5150) and the processor just starts executing code in it after reset.
The Alpha (or at least this AlphaStation 500 - although I think they mostly worked like this) is different.
SROM
There is a serial ROM (SROM) on the main board, and after reset, some logic internal to the CPU kicks in to generate a clock pulse. This drives an (external) counter, which provides consecutive addresses into the ROM. The 1-bit output of the ROM is sent into the processor, in sync with the clock pulse. The Alpha processor stores this data in its internal Instruction Cache. Once the code load is complete, the processor then executes the code, from its cache. The code is just enough to get the processor to configure its external memory bus, and find a memory-mapped parallel ROM, which it will then hand-over execution to.
But wait, how do you find a 1-bit wide ROM chip? Aren't most ROM chips at least 8 bits wide? Yes, they are.
SROM Image selection
The AlphaStation 500 mainboard has a series of eight jumper positions, and you are supposed to fit a jumper to exactly one of them. In fact, if you tried to fit more than one, the machine wouldn't boot.
The SROM chip actually contains eight images multiplexed together - each byte you load from the ROM contains one bit from each of eight images. The jumpers control which of the eight data bits on the ROM is actually connected to the serial input on the processor.
The SROM images on my machine are:
Jumper
Description
J11
Power up
J12
Mini console
J13
Floppy loader
J14
Mem test
J15
N/A
J16
N/A
J17
MCHK Mini Console
J19
No init mini console
So, given I apparently have RAM problems, I should
in theory
be able to move the jumper from J11 to J12, and see some kind of
'Mini console'
driven entirely by the processor running from internal I-Cache and its 32 internal registers, even with no RAM fitted.
But, I don't. Or at least, if there's a console, I can't find it. I read that it should be on the same pins that are used for loading the SROM into the chip, but I don't see any UART traffic there.
There is
some
SROM source code on The Internet, in a
pack designed for manufacturers making Alpha-based computers
using the OEM AlphaPC mainboards that Digital used to sell. But I don't know if it is anything like what's on my AlphaStation.
Maybe there's a way to look at the SROM code and work out what it should be doing?
Splitting the SROM
What is in my SROM chip? Well it's an Am27C010 in a PLCC socket, so I pulled it out, popped it into a TL866-II flash programmer and dumped it.
Download it
here
.
Remember, this is eight streams multiplexed together, so we need to break them apart. This is non-trivial because, if each byte has one bit from the chosen image in it, is the first bit the most-significant bit in a byte, or the least significant bit in a byte?
Because I wasn't sure exactly how this worked, I hacked around in Python and I think I have it right.
f =
open
("
am27c010_image_alphastation500.bin
", "
rb
")
contents = f.
read
()
for
image
in
range
(
0
,
8
):
count =
0
acc =
0
data = []
for
b
in
contents:
bit = (b >> image) &
1
# Loading bits in from the top, so the first bit
# ends up as the LSB
acc >>=
1
acc |= (bit <<
7
)
count = count +
1
if
count ==
8
:
data.
append
(acc)
acc =
0
count =
0
o =
open
(
f
"
srom_
{image}
.bin
", "
wb
")
o.
truncate
()
o.
write
(
bytes
(data))
o

data.title: We asked camera companies why their RAW formats are all different and confusing
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了为什么不同相机公司的RAW格式各不相同且令人困惑。尽管存在一种通用的开放源代码格式——DNG（数字负片），但只有少数相机使用它。大多数相机使用专有格式，如佳能的CR3、尼康的NEF和索尼的ARW，导致兼容性问题。Adobe推出的DNG格式旨在提供更大的灵活性和未来适应性，但由于大公司希望对图像处理流程有更强的控制，它们仍坚持使用自己的专有格式。专有格式允许相机制造商根据设备特性（如传感器和图像处理引擎）优化性能，而DNG因其开放性得到了一些小厂商和与Adobe有合作的公司采用。文章指出，这种格式混乱给软件开发者和早期相机使用者带来了不便。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[DNG与其他RAW格式的优缺点及其实际应用]

不同观点：
• **支持DNG者（vr46）**：vr46曾努力将所有数字图像转换为DNG格式，认为DNG是一种较为通用的格式，尤其是在多个相机品牌中使用。然而，实际应用中发现，即使使用DNG格式，在从Lightroom切换到Capture One后，编辑信息无法完全保留，导致失去了一些编辑记录。这表明DNG并没有完全实现其“通用”的承诺，特别是在不同软件之间的编辑兼容性上存在问题。

• **DNG局限性观点（vr46）**：尽管DNG在某些相机（如Pentax、Leica）中是原生支持的，但其他相机（如Canon、Fuji）仍然使用自己的专有RAW格式。这限制了DNG作为统一格式的优势。此外，DNG在跨软件使用时，特别是涉及编辑历史和元数据时，表现不如预期，导致用户在更换软件时可能丢失重要的编辑信息。

补充讨论：
• **JPEG作为最终版本**：vr46提到JPEG文件仍然是他图像的最终版本，这表明尽管RAW格式（包括DNG）在编辑和处理过程中具有优势，但最终交付或存档时，JPEG仍然被视为“确定版本”。

• **编辑信息跨平台兼容性问题**：争议的焦点在于DNG作为一种开放格式，虽然理论上应该在不同软件间保持编辑信息的兼容性，但实际应用中（如从Lightroom迁移到Capture One），编辑信息丢失，表明DNG在实际跨平台应用中的表现不如预期。

• **RAW处理器的更新和IQ改进**：用户希望能够利用新的RAW处理器和改进的图像质量（IQ），但由于格式和软件之间的兼容性问题，这一需求难以实现。这显示出在RAW格式选择上，用户需要在兼容性、编辑灵活性和图像质量之间做出权衡。

Part Of
Spec-tacular week
see all
Antonio G. Di Benedetto
is a reviewer covering laptops and the occasional gadget. He spent over 15 years in the photography industry before joining The Verge as a deals writer in 2021.
When you set up a new camera, or even go to take a picture on some smartphones, you’re presented with a key choice: JPG or RAW?
JPGs are ready to post just about anywhere, while RAWs yield an unfinished file filled with extra data that allows for much richer post-processing. That option for a RAW file (and even the generic name, RAW) has been standardized across the camera industry — but despite that, the camera world has never actually settled on one standardized RAW format.
Most cameras capture RAW files in proprietary formats, like Canon’s CR3, Nikon’s NEF, and Sony’s ARW. The result is a world of compatibility issues. Photo editing software needs to specifically support not just each manufacturer’s file type but also make changes for each new camera that shoots it. That creates pain for app developers and early camera adopters who want to know that their preferred software will just work.
Adobe tried to solve this problem years ago with a universal RAW format, DNG (Digital Negative), which it open-sourced for anyone to use. A handful of camera manufacturers have since adopted DNG as their RAW format. But the largest names in the space still use their own proprietary files. And there’s no sign of that changing anytime soon.
Why have some camera brands adopted native DNG files?
Some smaller camera manufacturers have been using the DNG format for years, while others like Sigma have adopted it more recently. The whole point of DNG is to offer flexibility, ease of use, and ideally, a little more futureproofing — since the format is open to use and royalty-free.
DNG was created in 2004 by Thomas Knoll, one of the co-creators of Photoshop, and was based on the even older TIFF image specification. DNG is capable of holding additional camera metadata embedded within it. While other RAW formats are usually coupled with an XMP sidecar file for storing metadata, DNG is slightly streamlined since it’s just one file that allows nondestructive metadata edits within it.
DNG is nearly old enough to legally drink (in the US)
Regardless of which camera brand you use, a RAW processing workflow is mostly the same: you take a picture, import it to a computer, open and process the file using editing software, and then export a “finished” file in a universal format (like JPG) for sharing or printing. Where things often get the messiest is with software compatibility.
You can’t use just any software or photo app to edit a RAW file — you generally need specialized apps that support your specific format. Widely used consumer apps like Apple’s Photos and Google Photos have some RAW support, but it’s frankly a bit janky. It’s best to use software like
Adobe’s Creative Cloud
,
Capture One
,
Photo Mechanic
, or
Darktable
.
Some camera manufacturers offer their own software. But ask most photographers, and they’ll likely steer you toward the third-party apps.
And there’s the big advantage for DNG. Because it’s an open standard, there’s wider third-party app support. That makes it a more turnkey solution for camera makers. It therefore makes sense that smaller manufacturers (Pentax, Ricoh, Leica, etc.) or ones with closer ties to Adobe (Apple) use it.
What are the advantages of a proprietary RAW format versus an open one like DNG?
Larger camera companies know that app developers will rush to support their latest features, letting them stick with their own RAW formats. A proprietary RAW format offers tighter control over the image pipeline direct from a manufacturer’s camera, from the point of capture to the files you’re editing on your computer.
That’s the sentiment I got from multiple camera company reps who gave me feedback when I asked them why they stuck with their proprietary format. Here are some of the answers I got when asked why they go with proprietary options:
Sony:
Michael Bubolo and Ryoko Noguchi of Sony’s product teams tell
The Verge
that Sony Alpha cameras use a proprietary ARW format “to maximize performance based on device characteristics such as the image sensor and image processing engine.”
Panasonic:
“A propri

data.title: NOAA Weather will delete websites using Amazon, Google cloud services Saturday
data.author: ck2
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：NOAA（美国国家海洋和大气管理局）云服务合同终止及其影响

不同观点：
• Kristopolous认为，NOAA正在进行的这项工作是错误的，并将此举形容为“死亡崇拜”，反映出对政府决策的强烈不满。
• Ryandvm关注NOAA的公共数据源是否会因合同终止而下线，担心NOAA在AWS上的公开数据流会消失。
• Feraloink对合同提前终止且没有公布替代方案表示担忧，认为这反映了政府领导能力的不足，并强调NOAA的研究对公众的重要性。
• Financetechbro援引Project 2025文件，主张解散NOAA并将其职能私有化或转移至其他机构，认为NOAA的现有组织结构存在问题，应该通过商业化提高效率。
• Katelynsills怀疑这一行动与Nikhil Rajpal在NOAA的工作有关，特别是他与Google的互动，质疑此举的动机和破坏性。
• 9283409232认为，这一计划的目的是将天气预报服务私有化，并将国家的利益出卖给私人公司如Accuweather。
• Tmshapland对此表示悲哀，但未提出具体论据。
• NoImmatureAdHom提出疑问，是否取消合同有合理的理由，希望了解合同条款是否公平，以及政府是否在支付合理费用，而不是仅仅基于党派立场做出反应。
• Ck2特别关注Space Weather网站是否会下线，认为这一决定将带来巨大损失，且没有必要。
• Superkuh批评NOAA从2015年开始转向现代 web 开发技术，认为如果继续使用以前的静态网页技术，就不会出现当前的问题，暗示技术选择不当是导致当前困境的原因之一。
• Dboreham澄清，合同终止仅影响NOAA研究部门的网站和服务，不会影响天气服务的核心数据流，反驳了一些误解。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于NOAA合同终止是否合理及其潜在影响。一部分人担心公众无法再获取重要的科学数据，另一部分人则认为NOAA的组织和运作存在问题，需要改革或私有化。
- 技术选择的讨论，特别是从静态网页转向现代 web 应用的决策，也被认为是导致当前问题的原因之一。
- 政治立场在讨论中起到一定作用，但也有评论者呼吁理性分析合同条款和实际影响，而非仅基于党派立场做出判断。

data.title: Show HN: Mermaid Chart VS Code Plugin: Mermaid.js Diagrams in Visual Studio Code
data.author: msfi
data.article_summary: 《Mermaid Chart VS Code插件：在Visual Studio Code中创建和编辑Mermaid.js图表》文章介绍了该插件的强大功能，帮助开发者在VS Code环境中直接创建和编辑Mermaid.js图表。主要特点包括无需账户即可编辑`.mmd`文件、自动文件识别和语法高亮、实时图表渲染与平移缩放、Markdown中嵌入图表、云同步和团队协作、离线编辑与Git版本控制，以及通过AI从代码生成图表。插件还支持灵活的编辑方式，可以在VS Code内或Mermaid平台上操作。开发者常用它来可视化DevOps流程、API通信、微服务架构等。安装简便，基本功能无需账户，高级协作功能需登录。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mermaid工具的应用和价值

不同观点：
• **支持Markdown集成的观点**：[mackenly] 认为Mermaid的价值在于其与Markdown的无缝集成，而非作为独立的文件格式使用。他强调Mermaid图表作为视觉辅助工具嵌入文档的价值，并指出当前扩展在语法高亮和Markdown预览支持方面的不足。

43581193.article_content:
The Trump administration has fired Timothy Haugh, the head of the National Security Agency and Cyber Command, several news publications reported overnight into Friday.
Haugh, a career military official, led the National Security Agency, the U.S.’ main wiretapping and intelligence gathering agency, for little more than a year after his appointment in February 2024 following his predecessor’s retirement. Haugh also oversaw Cyber Command, a military unit that conducts offensive cyber operations against U.S. adversaries.
The Washington Post
, which first reported the news, and
The New York Times
, said the firings come after right-wing activist Laura Loomer advocated for Haugh’s firing along with several other national security officials during a meeting with President Donald Trump in the Oval Office on Thursday.
NSA deputy director Wendy Noble, who served as the agency’s top civilian leader, was also let go,
according to reports
.
It’s not clear who is currently overseeing the NSA and Cyber Command following Haugh’s firing.
A spokesperson for The White House did not immediately comment on the reason for Haugh’s removal.
Contact us securely
Do you work at NSA or in government and know more? You can contact Zack Whittaker on Signal at zackwhittaker.1337 — and share documents securely with TechCrunch via
SecureDrop
.
Eddie Bennett, a spokesperson for the National Security Agency, deferred comment to the Department of Defense, which houses the NSA.
A spokesperson for the Department of Defense, who did not provide their name, told TechCrunch that the organization has “seen the reports but have nothing to offer at this time,” and that it will “provide more information when it becomes available.”
The move to oust one of the country’s top intelligence officials appeared to catch senior lawmakers overseeing the agency by surprise.
In a statement, Mark Warner, a Democrat senator from Virginia and vice-chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, called the news of Haugh’s firing “astonishing.”
“General Haugh has served our country in uniform, with honor and distinction, for more than 30 years,” said Warner. “At a time when the United States is facing unprecedented cyber threats, as the Salt Typhoon cyberattack from China has so clearly underscored, how does firing him make Americans any safer?,” he wrote, referring to a
series of long-running China-led hacks against U.S. phone and internet giants
that were discovered last year.
Warner also criticized the Trump administration for the firing while “still failing to hold any member of his team accountable” for sharing classified information about air strikes in Yemen in a Signal messaging group chat with several other senior cabinet-level officials, which
inadvertently included a journalist
.
Jim Himes, a Democrat congressman who heads the House’s intelligence committee, said in remarks that he was “deeply disturbed” by the decision to remove Haugh.
In March, The Wall Street Journal reported that Elon Musk, who
heads the Trump administration’s Department of Government Efficiency
, met with Haugh at the NSA’s headquarters in Fort Meade, Maryland. At the time, the NSA said the meeting was to ensure its priorities were aligned with the Trump administration.
Musk had previously called for an “overhaul” at the spy agency, but did not provide specifics.

data.author: imakwana
data.article_summary:
MIT的“安全硬件设计”课程（6.5950/6.5951）是一门开源课程，教授学生如何攻击现代CPU以及设计抵御这些攻击的架构。学生通过实战获得攻击真实处理器的经验，学习各种先进硬件攻击与防御技术。课程包括三个核心部分：

1. **思考（Think）**：通过讲座引导学生批判性思考硬件安全，内容涵盖微架构攻击、侧信道、瞬态执行攻击（如Spectre、Meltdown）、物理安全、可信执行环境等。
   
2. **玩耍（Play）**：通过互动式辅导课和Capture-the-Flag（CTF）游戏，让学生在竞赛中实践课程材料。

3. **实践（Do）**：在实验室中，学生在真实硬件上实施攻击，如缓存侧信道、Spectre、Rowhammer等，无需模拟器。

所有实验均为开源，可免费使用，但需联系课程团队获取教师解决方案。每年课程内容会根据硬件安全研究动态更新。

Secure Hardware Design
MIT’s Secure Hardware Design Class (6.5950/6.5951) is an open-source course that teaches students both how to attack modern CPUs and design architectures resilient to those attacks. Students gain hands-on experience hacking real processors and are taught various state-of-the-art hardware attacks and defenses.
This course is the culmination of multiple years of work.
Browse our story here
.
Meet the Team
Secure Hardware Design is the culmination of years of effort by a team of students. Say “hello” to the people behind it!
Think, Play, Do.
Our course philosophy involves three pillars- Think, Play, Do.‍
Think
In Lecture, we encourage students to think critically about hardware security as a part of greater systems. Our lectures are designed to guide critical thinking and engagement with the research literature.
Topic
Lecture Materials
Microarchitectural Attacks
Side channels introduction 🔨
Cache side channel deep dive 🔨
Transient execution attacks (Spectre, Meltdown)
Side channel defenses
Physical security
Hardware Security Modules (HSM)
Physical Attacks (Power analysis, EM, fault injection) 🔨
Rowhammer
Hardware support for software security
Trusted Execution Environment (TEE)
Memory safety mechanisms 🔨
Tools for security assurance
Fuzzing, formal verification 🔨
The 🔨 icon means this lecture features an in-class demo.
Please send requests for powerpoint files to
Mengjia
.
Play
In Recitation, we encourage students to play with the course materials through interactive hands-on games. Our recitations consist of interactive learning sessions, leveraging the Capture-the-Flag (CTF) format for friendly competitions amongst students. Students team up and work with their peers to conquer various challenges together.‍
Topic
Content
Format
C/C++ Recitation
A brief refresher on C/ C++ syntax and useful features.
CTF
Cache Attack Recitation
A visual overview of prime+probe on a custom RISC-V CPU.
Group Learning
Physical Attacks Recitation
Students work together to implement a timing side channel against real microcontrollers.
CTF
RISC-V System Programming Recitation
Overview of the privileged ISA specification for RISC-V with emphasis on exception handling and interrupt conditions.
CTF
Formal Verification Recitation
Students learn the basics of formal verification techniques.
Group Learning
Do
In Labs, students have a chance to actually put the concepts from class to work. The attack labs involve implementing attacks taught in class on real hardware. No simulators, no trickery, no nonsense. Real implementations on real hardware.‍
“How can I use your materials in my class?”
Every year, we update our course to reflect the ever-changing landscape of research in the hardware security world. All of these labs are open-source and free to use. Just shoot us an email at
hw-sec-lab-dev
at mit dot edu before doing so, so we can give you the instructor’s solutions and starter gradebook. If you do use our materials in your class, make sure to attribute us on your class webpage.
Lab
Difficulty
Setup
Cache Side Channels
Hard
x86_64 Linux server. Some tuning required. We use Cascade Lake.
Spectre
Medium
x86_64 Linux server.
Website Fingerprinting
Easy
Any modern web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari).
Rowhammer

ASLR Bypasses

x86_64 Linux server.
CPU Fuzzing

x86_64 Linux server.
Cache Side Channels (Dead Drop)
Students start with building primitives to measure cache access latencies and examine microarchitecture details. Next, they will implement Prime+Probe on a modern cache hierarchy, requiring a thorough understanding of cache geometry. Finally, they implement a covert channel chat client, demonstrating mastery over creating contention on set associative structures.
Spectre
Students implement a Flush+Reload attack against shared memory between userspace and kernelspace. Then, they extend their attack to work under speculation in increasingly difficult exploitation scenarios to leak kernel memory back to userspace.
Website Fingerprinting
We start with teaching students to implement a cache occupancy attack using Javascript to profile different websites. Next, the students are guided to use machine learning to distinguish these websites based on their traces collected using JavaScripts. Finally, we ask the students to slightly change the attack and think about the root causes of the attack.
Rowhammer
Students learn the essential steps towards implementing Rowhammer in the wild. We guide the students to go through the two level address translation: virtual address -> physical address -> DRAM location. The students are first given the physical address of vulnerable rows and hammer rows and they will quickly see bit flips in the wild. Then the students are asked to reverse engineering some missing pieces of DRAM banking functions to search for unknown vulnerable rows.

MIT的“安全硬件设计”课程（6.5950/6.5951）是一门开源课程，教授学生如何攻击现代CPU以及设计抵御这些攻击的架构。学生通过实战获得攻击真实处理器的经验，学习各种先进硬件攻击与防御技术。课程包括三个核心部分：

1. **思考（Think）**：通过讲座引导学生批判性思考硬件安全，内容涵盖微架构攻击、侧信道、瞬态执行攻击（如Spectre、Meltdown）、物理安全、可信执行环境等。
   
2. **玩耍（Play）**：通过互动式辅导课和Capture-the-Flag（CTF）游戏，让学生在竞赛中实践课程材料。

3. **实践（Do）**：在实验室中，学生在真实硬件上实施攻击，如缓存侧信道、Spectre、Rowhammer等，无需模拟器。

所有实验均为开源，可免费使用，但需联系课程团队获取教师解决方案。每年课程内容会根据硬件安全研究动态更新。

data.title: Stop syncing everything
data.author: neilk
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了Graft，一个开源的事务存储引擎，旨在解决部分数据同步问题，特别适用于边缘设备和离线环境。传统的物理复制简单但需同步所有更改，包括已被丢弃的；而逻辑复制虽高效但复杂，难以保持强一致性。Graft结合了两者的优点，支持懒同步和部分复制，且保证强一致性和水平扩展性。它适用于离线优先、跨平台同步、无状态多写入副本等场景，并能复制任意数据类型。Graft通过“卷”和“快照”机制实现高效同步，客户端只需获取自上次同步以来的更改元数据，再决定需要获取哪些数据，从而实现部分复制。这使得Graft在资源受限的环境中也能有效工作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Graft一致性模型及其在数据同步和冲突处理方面的设计和实现

不同观点：
• [kiitos] 认为Graft的"commit"模型存在问题。他指出，Graft的API提供的单次提交操作在本地成功后，可能在异步远程提交时失败，导致需要回滚先前基于该提交的操作。这种模型混淆了“本地提交”和“异步验证提交”的概念，让人困惑。
• [chacham15] 将Graft的一致性模型比作Git，指出了潜在的冲突问题，尤其是读取冲突。他举例说明两个并发事务可能在没有页面冲突的情况下产生错误结果，建议跟踪事务中读取的页面以解决此问题。
• [0xbadcafebee] 对分布式数据系统的通用解决方案持怀疑态度，认为Graft在边缘设备和不可靠网络环境下可能面临数据获取不及时的问题。他还指出，分布式关系数据库在ACID特性上存在局限性，CRDTs等独立副本处理方法可能更合适。
• [snickell] 赞赏Graft的通用低层级设计，认为这种方法在实践中的稳健性可能会使其应用于SQLite之外的更多场景。同时，他强调具体经验对指导通用解决方案的重要性。
• [stavros] 强调了同步层的重要性，期望有一个无需开发者额外工作的同步解决方案，使用户能够自主管理同步服务器，降低订阅费用。
• [wim] 分享了他们为离线优先的笔记应用开发同步引擎的经验，指出树结构的冲突处理挑战，并询问Graft如何定义和处理这些快照。
• [londons_explore] 提出在慢速连接下，初始同步可能需要大量数据传输，建议采用混合方法，在检测到慢速同步时直接向服务器发送查询。
• [krick] 对Graft的实际功能感到困惑，认为文档和示例不足，尤其是对于冲突处理方面的具体应用场景不明确。

补充讨论：
• [carlsverre] 作为Graft的作者，感谢了社区的支持，并提供了更多关于Graft的深入讨论链接，邀请用户进一步了解Graft的实现细节。
• [conradev] 和 [vladstudio] 分别提供了与其他类似工具和系统的比较，扩展了关于Graft设计选择的讨论背景。
• [presentation] 和 [smitty1e] 提供了额外的资源和幽默评论，增加了讨论的广度和趣味性。

争议焦点：
• Graft的"commit"模型是否清晰，尤其是本地提交和异步验证的关系。
• 如何有效地处理和检测冲突，特别是在读取冲突和复杂数据结构的情况下。
• 在不可靠网络条件下，Graft的实用性和数据获取策略。
• Graft文档和示例的清晰度以及对实际应用场景的指导。

Stop syncing everything
Carl Sverre
March 2025
Partial replication sounds easy—just sync the data your app needs, right? But choosing an approach is tricky: logical replication precisely tracks every change, complicating strong consistency, while physical replication avoids that complexity but requires syncing every change, even discarded ones.
What if your app could combine the simplicity of physical replication with the efficiency of logical replication?
That’s the key idea behind
Graft
, the open-source transactional storage engine I’m launching today. It’s designed specifically for lazy, partial replication with strong consistency, horizontal scalability, and object storage durability.
Rather watch than read?
My
Vancouver Systems talk
explains Graft visually.
Graft is designed with the following
use cases
in mind:
Offline-first & mobile apps
:
Simplify development
and improve reliability by offloading replication and storage to Graft.
Cross-platform sync
: Share data smoothly across devices, browsers, and platforms without vendor lock-in.
Stateless multi-writer replicas
: Deploy replicas anywhere, including serverless and embedded environments.
Any data type
: Replicate databases, files, or custom formats—all with strong consistency.
I first discovered the need for Graft while building
SQLSync
. SQLSync is a frontend optimized database stack built on top of
SQLite
with a synchronization engine powered by ideas from Git and distributed systems. SQLSync makes multiplayer SQLite databases a reality, powering interactive apps that run directly in your browser.
However, SQLSync replicates the entire log of changes to every client—similar to how some databases implement physical replication. While this approach works fine on servers, it’s poorly suited to the constraints of edge and browser environments.
After shipping SQLSync, I decided to find a replication solution more suited to the edge. I needed something that could:
Let clients
sync at their own pace
Sync only what they need
Sync from anywhere
, including the edge and offline devices
Replicate
arbitrary data
1
All while providing
strong consistency guarantees
.
That didn’t exist. So I built it.
#
A different approach to edge replication
If you’ve ever tried to keep data in sync across clients and servers, you know it’s harder than it sounds. Most existing solutions fall into one of two camps:
Full replication
, which syncs the entire dataset to each client—not practical for constrained environments like serverless functions or web apps.
Schema-aware diffs
, like
Change Data Capture (CDC)
or
Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDTs)
, which track logical changes at the row or field level—but require deep application integration and don’t generalize to arbitrary data.
Graft takes a different path.
Like full replication, Graft is schema-agnostic. It doesn’t know or care what kind of data you’re storing—it just replicates bytes
2
. But instead of sending all the data, it behaves more like logical replication: clients receive a compact description of what’s changed since their last sync.
At the core of this model is the Volume: a sparse, ordered collection of fixed-size Pages. Clients interact with Volumes through a transactional API, reading and writing at specific Snapshots. Under the hood, Graft persists and replicates only what’s necessary—using object storage as a durable, scalable backend.
The result is a system that’s lazy, partial, edge-capable, and consistent.
Want to try the managed version of Graft?
Join the waitlist to get early access:
Sign up here →
Each of these properties deserves a closer look—let’s unpack them one by one.
#
Lazy: Sync at your own pace
Graft is designed for the real world—where edge clients wake up occasionally, face unreliable networks, and run in short-lived, resource-constrained environments. Instead of relying on continuous replication, clients choose
when
to sync, and Graft makes it easy to fast forward to the latest snapshot.
That sync starts with a simple question:
what changed since my last snapshot?
The server responds with a
graft
—a compact bitset of page indexes that have changed across all commits since that snapshot
3
. This is where the project gets its name: a
graft
attaches new changes to an existing snapshot—like grafting a branch onto a tree. They act as a guide, informing the
client which pages can be reused and which need to be fetched if needed.
Critically, when a client pulls a
graft
from the server, it doesn’t receive any actual data—only metadata about what changed. This gives the client full control over what to fetch and when, laying the foundation for partial replication.
#
Partial: Sync only what’s needed
When you’re building for edge environments—browser tabs, mobile apps, serverless functions—you can’t afford to download the entire dataset just to serve a handful of queries. That’s where partial replication comes in.

, it knows exactly what’s changed. It can

data.title: Show HN: OpenNutrition – A free, public nutrition database
data.author: joshdickson
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一款重新构想的营养搜索工具，具有即时结果、开源和通过AI增强准确性的特点。用户可以搜索食物的营养信息，同时该工具注重隐私保护并提供了使用条款。这一工具旨在为用户提供快速、准确且透明的营养数据查询服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenNutrition应用的营养数据生成和验证方法，及其可靠性和透明度

不同观点：
• Cheer2171认为通过LLM（大语言模型）生成的营养数据是对科学方法的侮辱，认为LLM堆叠无法得出关于世界的真理，并质疑该方法的科学性。
• yamihere指出LLM也可能不可靠，质疑如何确保新内容的权威性和准确性，并怀疑验证步骤是否也是由LLM创建，同时对产品 minimizing AI aspect 的市场策略表示怀疑。
• bhatfiel和johnisgood通过具体例子（如蜂蜜烤燕麦和鸡蛋的胆碱含量）指出数据的准确性问题，质疑LLM生成的营养数据是否可靠。
• lm28469关注技术问题，指出Safari上的搜索功能存在bug，影响用户体验。

补充讨论：
• diggan推荐了Yuka.io作为替代方案，指出其在欧洲和美国产品的良好使用体验，并强调其免费功能和用户决定年费的模式。
• briandoll提到已有的开放营养数据源，如Cronometer，暗示用户已有其他选择。
• adamas将OpenNutrition与OpenFoodFacts进行比较，询问其主要区别。
• octotep对微量营养素的估算方法感兴趣，并希望了解更多细节。
• monkburger提醒注意食品数据库的准确性受限于食品标签法的规定，指出即便最好意图的数据库也受限于不完整或不准确的营养信息。
• Rooster61询问API和应用聚焦问题，希望有一个动态食谱扫描功能，并质疑为何主要功能存在于移动端而非SaaS选项。
• papa_bear分享了类似项目的经验，指出数据质量问题，并强调即便不精确的数据也能提供80%的摄入跟踪效益。
• neilv对许可条款和名称表示不满，认为“开放”一词被商业公司使用不当，并指出其隐私和安全问题。
• kekub推荐瑞士食品成分数据库作为验证LLM方法的良好资源。
• reverendsteveii对应用的界面和功能提出建议，如按比例调整份量和自动抓取食谱营养信息。

争议焦点：
• LLM生成营养数据的可靠性和验证方法的有效性。
• 市场策略中minimizing AI aspect是否合适。
• 数据准确性和来源的透明度。
• 应用聚焦于移动端而非SaaS选项的合理性。

Company description
Thunder Compute is a Y-Combinator backed AI-infrastructure startup. We are creating technology to improve GPU utilization through sharing and oversubscription at the CUDA API layer.
Our core software lets us network-attach GPUs over TCP. This lets us allocate compute wherever it is needed most, leading to utilization gains of 5x+, with minimal performance overhead. We believe servers using dedicated GPUs is archaic, and plan to scale our virtualization software to every data center GPU in the world.
This is a $100B+ opportunity, with a problem that uniquely boils down to technical execution. In this systems engineering role, you would be employee #2, working on our core virtualization software.
If you are a top 0.1% systems engineer, looking for a problem that can be solved through sheer technical execution, this is the single highest potential opportunity on the market.
Job description
You will report directly to Co-founder and CTO Brian (ex-citadel quant dev). You likely have prior experience in quant dev, at NVIDIA, or similar. You are fed up working as a cog in a machine, you’d rather make a bet on your technical chops and change the world than take the $600K TC alternatives sitting in front of you.
If this role is a fit, you know who you are.

This roll is full-time, on-site at our headquarters in Atlanta, GA, salaried with stock options. Thunder GPU, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer, and adheres to all applicable employment laws.

Thunder Compute is a cloud computing platform that makes GPUs cheaper and easier to use. We do this with proprietary software to virtualize GPUs over a network.

主要讨论点：美国是否需要改变思维以建设与其他发达国家媲美的高铁系统，以及美国主要城市与中国的城市发展对比。

不同观点：
• [redacted_ib] 认为，美国需要改变思维方式，才能建设与发达国家水平相当的高速铁路系统。他暗示美国在基础设施方面落后于其他国家，特别是高铁方面。
• [DeathArrow] 则将讨论引向城市外观和治安问题，认为像西雅图和旧金山等城市虽然有高科技产业，但城市环境和治安状况不佳，相较于中国深圳等城市，显得不够先进，甚至给人一种破败的印象。

补充讨论：
• [redacted_ib] 的观点集中在基础设施建设，尤其是高铁系统，并暗示美国在交通系统方面需要追赶其他国家。
• [DeathArrow] 的观点则更多关注城市的外观、治安以及社会问题，认为高科技产业并不能掩盖城市内部的社会问题。
• 争议的焦点在于美国城市是否真的在基础设施和社会问题方面落后于中国城市，以及这些因素如何影响一个国家整体的发展水平和国际形象。

Shenzhen is China’s leading high-tech hub. The once obscure fishing village became a pillar of the global economy thanks to its proximity to Hong Kong and to being designated a Special Economic Zone in the earliest days of Deng’s reforms, plus some other smart choices and good luck. Part and parcel of that economic transformation is that the city has
physically
transformed from
looking like a poor fishing village to looking like a major 21st-century city
.
Photos of Shenzhen via
PMA Magazine
The US can’t point to any specific economic transformation as dramatic as Shenzhen’s for the simple reason that absolutely nowhere in the United States of America was as poor in 1982 as Shenzhen was. But we absolutely do have places that have become home to world-leading technology companies. And it’s not just that those places haven’t transformed to the extent Shenzhen has (that’s a base effect); it’s that Seattle and San Francisco and nearby Silicon Valley don’t
look
nearly as advanced and high-tech as Shenzhen does.
That’s because in these cities, and basically all American cities, it is fundamentally illegal to enact large-scale transformation of the built environment within the existing footprint of development.
Some parts of the country make it relatively easy to transform farmland into single-family homes and strip malls, and in those places you see growing metro areas. Other parts of the country restrict both kinds of growth. But nowhere allows for the physical transformation of an existing community. Change is treated as per se bad — like air pollution — and something that regulators should try to prevent. And yet everyone who looks at China’s cutting edge coastal cities comes away impressed and borderline incredulous that China’s GDP per capita is still so much lower than America’s.
I wrote on Tuesday about tariffs as a
misguided effort to create male-coded blue collar work through regulations that make most people poorer
.
But today, let’s think about Shenzhen.

data.title: Kerosene did not save the sperm whale (2024)
data.author: baud147258
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于鲸油与煤油对抹香鲸种群影响的讨论

不同观点：
• **creddit的观点**：指出原文中关于19世纪鲸鱼捕捞加工的错误。creddit认为，即使在19世纪，捕鲸者已经在海上加工捕获的鲸鱼，而不是将鲸鱼拖回陆地加工，尽管当时的加工效率可能不如现代。

• **RandallBrown的观点**：认为煤油确实拯救了抹香鲸，依据是捕鲸活动在煤油出现后减少了约60年，直到汽车普及后才再次上升。RandallBrown提到电灯照明可能也对鲸油需求下降起了作用。

• **hinkley的观点**：通过一个关于AWS和其竞争者的类比，提出一些商业行为中的复杂动机。hinkley认为，就像亚马逊资助AWS的竞争者一样，鲸油灯的销售者可能会欢迎煤油作为替代燃料，因为这给消费者一种“总有其他选择”的感觉，从而延缓了对鲸油需求下降的速度。

• **RcouF1uZ4gsC的观点**：明确支持煤油拯救了抹香鲸的观点，并补充了鲸油不仅用于照明，还用于润滑海军时钟、制药、油漆和炸药等用途。RcouF1uZ4gsC指出，煤油替代了低价值、高价格敏感度的照明用途，使得普通大众不再关心鲸油，而高价值用途的使用者有能力进行研发以找到替代品。

补充讨论：
• **wazoox的观点**：对《Material World》一书表示赞赏，并希望作者能就其他资源再写一本书，未直接参与到煤油与鲸油的讨论中。

• **TheBlight的观点**：通过类比太阳能板和石油开采，认为即使有替代技术出现，也不一定会立即阻止人们继续使用传统资源，暗示即使煤油出现，也不一定立即拯救了抹香鲸。

争议焦点：
• 争议的核心在于煤油是否真正拯救了抹香鲸，以及替代技术对传统资源使用的影响程度。RandallBrown和RcouF1uZ4gsC支持煤油的正面作用，而TheBlight则提出替代技术未必立即见效的质疑。

data.author: duck
data.article_summary: Cinc是一套由Chef Software Inc.提供的开源软件的免费发行版。其主要项目包括：Cinc Client（基于Chef Infra）、Cinc Workstation（基于Chef Workstation）、Cinc Auditor（基于Chef InSpec）和Cinc Server（基于Chef Infra Server）。即将推出Cinc Packager（基于Chef Habitat）。用户可以通过社区Slack频道#community-distros与开发团队交流，获取更多项目详情或更新可关注其博客。

data.title: The Curse of Ayn Rand's Heir
data.author: Michelangelo11
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了哲学家艾恩·兰德（Ayn Rand）的葬礼及其遗产继承问题。兰德的葬礼更像是一场庆祝，数百名仰慕者出席，现场播放着她喜爱的音乐，摆满了鲜艳的花卉和美元符号形状的花饰。她的遗产继承人莱昂纳德·佩科夫（Leonard Peikoff）自青少年时期起便追随兰德，对她极为忠诚。尽管兰德曾考虑过其他继承人，但最终因与其他追随者决裂，佩科夫成为其唯一继承人。佩科夫负责管理兰德的财产和其“客观主义”哲学的传播，这带来了巨大的影响力和经济收益。然而，捍卫兰德遗产的过程引发了与其他客观主义者的冲突，甚至导致佩科夫与女儿陷入痛苦的法律纠纷，使他的晚年生活陷入困境。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Objectivism哲学的实践与理论之间的矛盾，及其代表人物Peikoff的生活引发的讨论

不同观点：
• [gcp123] 认为Peikoff的生活轨迹充满了讽刺，他一生致力于提倡极端独立性的Objectivism哲学，但却在现实中表现出对他人的依赖，先是对Rand，现在是对其照顾者兼妻子。评论还指出，Objectivism在实践中与其宣扬的理性与独立性相矛盾，运动中的核心问题是表面宣扬个人主义，实际却要求一致性与忠诚。评论进一步将Peikoff与其女儿在遗产问题上的争端与《阿特拉斯耸耸肩》中的情节相比较，指出其中的相似性。

• [teekert] 表达了对《阿特拉斯耸耸肩》的强烈共鸣，认为小说中的理想角色和不妥协的世界观为自己带来了能量和解放感。尽管意识到小说中的角色可能过于理想化，且没有孩子的生活让其世界观显得不现实，但Rand的哲学帮助他从过去受限的基督教世界观中解放出来。他承认任何教条都是不好的，但Rand的哲学通过理性寻求真理的承诺对他产生了持久吸引力。

• [jonfw] 不认同所谓的讽刺，指出Rand的作品中经常探讨继承问题，主人公往往也是财富的继承者，因此Peikoff“继承”Rand的遗产并不矛盾。他认为文章更关注的是将哲学极端化所带来的社会危险，以及如何在老年时避免被利用的问题。

• [greener_grass] 提供了一个外部资源，推荐了一个与Murray Rothbard相关的戏剧，可能暗示对Objectivism及相关讨论有其他视角。

I
f not for
the open casket, Ayn Rand’s funeral might have been confused for a party. On March 8, 1982, hundreds of admirers lined up outside a funeral home on Manhattan’s Upper East Side to pay their respects to the author and philosopher, basking in their shared love for the queen of selfishness. Inside, a phonograph played jovial turn-of-the-century tunes—Rand called it her “tiddlywink music”—at high volume. Colorful bouquets lined the room, including a six-foot-tall floral arrangement in the shape of a dollar sign.
Off to the side, perched on a red plush couch, a man in his late 40s named Leonard Peikoff held court. Skinny and energetic, with groomed hair and thick glasses, he looked every bit the tweedy philosophy professor. He greeted well-wishers and answered questions about Rand’s remarkable life and singular philosophy. A visitor unfamiliar with Rand’s personal history might have assumed he was her son.
In some ways, he was. Peikoff had attached himself to Rand more than 30 years earlier, when he was just a teenager, and never let go. Both were immigrants of Russian Jewish extraction—she from Russia itself, he by way of Canada—who felt more at home in the salons of New York City than in their countries of origin. Rand called him by the affectionate diminutive “Leonush.” They shared an intensity, a ferocious intellectualism, a love of cigarettes and Viennese operetta, and a combustible mix of ego and insecurity. Rand had demanded total loyalty of her disciples, and Peikoff was the most loyal of all. He had stood by her through ups and downs: her struggle to write her magnum opus,
Atlas Shrugged
; the triumph of publication; the book’s
dismissive critical reception
; and her falling out with some of her closest allies.
Peikoff’s devotion paid off: Rand designated him as her sole heir. He was not Rand’s original choice; she had promised her inheritance to other followers over the years. But by the time she died, she had alienated all of them. Peikoff was one of the only close friends Rand had left—the person she turned to for day-to-day help, for comfort, and for affirmation that she and her work still mattered.
The person in charge of her property—her diaries, her letters, the copyrights to her books—would wield great power over how Rand would be remembered.
Managing Rand’s estate would entail more than handling her personal property. By the end of her life, her
philosophy of objectivism
—which proclaims the glory of individualism and the evils of altruism—had become a full-blown movement, and it was now Peikoff’s job to guide it forward. Rand’s books sold in the millions, despite their imposing heft. Her angular face and enormous eyes were all over magazines and TV sets in the ’60s and ’70s, and her eccentric charm won over talk-show hosts like Johnny Carson and Phil Donahue. But Rand’s life had always been a mystery. She spoke little of her upbringing in Russia and kept her personal affairs private. The gap between her cultural ubiquity and the scarcity of information about her created a fascination bordering on obsession among both fans and detractors. The person in charge of her property—her diaries, her letters, the copyrights to her books—would wield great power over how Rand would be remembered.

Left:
Rand in 1957, the year
Atlas Shrugged
was published.
Right:

The inheritance was also a windfall for Peikoff. Rand’s estate was worth an estimated half a million dollars at the time of her death, and her copyrights would eventually bring in hundreds of thousands of dollars a year in royalties. Peikoff, a lifelong advocate of autonomy and self-reliance, would never have to worry about money again.
After the funeral service, Peikoff asked to be left alone with the casket. Like Rand, he was a strident atheist; he knew she couldn’t hear him. Still, he spoke aloud to her, promising that he would live up to the responsibility she’d bestowed on him. He swore to keep her philosophy “pure,” and to make sure that her work lived on. “It was a vow,” he later said, “which I spent the rest of my life carrying out.”
Fulfilling that promise would come at a cost. His quest to defend Rand’s legacy would provoke nasty brawls with other objectivists. And his stewardship of her estate would lead to a painful conflict closer to home: Four decades after Rand’s death, Peikoff has found himself mired in an ugly legal battle with his own daughter. data.title: Growing Buffers to Avoid Copying Data
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在软件项目中避免数据拷贝以提升性能的方法，特别关注操作系统层面的支持。在C语言中，`realloc`函数可以在原地扩展或缩小内存，避免数据拷贝，但在C++中没有类似功能，只能使用`new`和`delete`。对于非平凡可复制类型，甚至不能使用`realloc`，需要手动构造和销毁对象。

为解决此问题，文章提出实现一个`resize_buffer`函数，尝试在原地调整缓冲区大小。对于小于内存页的缓冲区，这种方法可能导致巨大内存开销。而对于大缓冲区，可以通过操作系统的虚拟内存功能实现扩展。

在Linux上，使用`mmap`系统调用分配内存，并通过指定`base_addr`来确保缓冲区可扩展性。文章还提到在测试环境中，让系统自动选择地址会导致扩展失败，因此必须手动提供地址。

最后，文章邀请读者联系Johnny’s Software Lab LLC讨论性能问题或获取培训。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于内存管理、动态内存分配及其实现优化的讨论

不同观点：
• [wilted-iris] 认为测量次数过少（仅十次）使得数据的可信度存疑，指出数据可能不足。
• [kazinator] 提出在使用 `realloc` 时应通过自定义的 `sane_realloc` 函数来处理边界情况，以避免 ISO C 中 `realloc` 函数的异常行为。他详细描述了 `sane_realloc` 的实现，并指出 `malloc(0)` 不一定返回 `null`，并给出了相应的解决方案。
• [hummusandsushi] 认为 C++ 的特性经常互相冲突，尤其是在面向对象特性与传统 C 代码结合时，这些额外的特性并没有增加太多价值，反而限制了程序员的自由。
• [Dwedit] 讨论了使用 `VirtualAlloc` 动态分配内存的另一种方法，即通过内存映射文件将同一内存页映射到不同位置，从而避免不连续内存块的复制操作。不过他也提到，系统调用有额外的开销（如 Meltdown/Spectre 缓解措施），因此避免内存复制未必总是能带来性能优势。
• [edoceo] 分享了一个在 ASP3/IIS 时代的实际案例，通过预分配缓冲区（如实现 `StringBuffer`）显著提升了运行时性能（提升了500%），尽管内存使用量增加了10%。
• [xeonmc] 提到了在 Windows 10 及以上版本中，可以使用 `VirtualAlloc2`，它允许保留占位符并分配 64k 页面，提供了更灵活的内存分配选项。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于不同内存分配和管理方式的优劣。`kazinator` 强调了 `realloc` 函数的边界问题，并给出了优化方案；`hummusandsushi` 对 C++ 特性持批评态度，认为其在实际应用中限制了程序员；`Dwedit` 和 `edoceo` 提供了关于内存管理和优化的实际案例，强调了内存管理对性能的影响；`xeonmc` 补充了在现代 Windows 系统中更先进的内存分配方法。

We at
Johnny’s Software Lab LLC
are experts in performance. If performance is in any way concern in your software project, feel free to
contact us
.
Copying data can be expensive in some cases, especially since it it doesn’t change the data, it’s just moves it. Therefore we, engineers interested in performance, want to avoid copying data as much as possible.
We already talked about
avoiding data copying in C++
earlier. In that post, we talked about what mechanism C++ has to offer when it comes to avoiding or minimizing copying. In this post, we focus more on what the operating system can give us to avoid data copying.
A small introduction
Among memory allocation functions in C library, one function is particular:
realloc
. This function allows us to grow or shrink a buffer allocated with
malloc
or
calloc
: if
realloc
can do it in place, it will avoid copying data. If not, then it will allocate a new buffer, copy the data there, and free the old buffer.
If you are using C, this is all that you need. In C++, things get complicated. C++ doesn’t have a dedicated
realloc
function. It only offers
new
and
delete
for the user. Containers use
std::allocator
to allocate memory, but again, no buffer growth is available there.
If you need your buffers growing, you can opt for custom container implementation with
realloc
. But, there is a problem of non trivially copyable types: some types cannot be copied using realloc, instead they need to be properly constructed and destroyed. Therefore, for some types,
realloc
is not even an option. Instead, a manual construct new-destroy old sequence is needed for the things to work correctly.
API for enlarging buffers
If we want to avoid copying in C++, we would need a function called
resize_buffer
with a following signature:
bool resize_buffer(void* ptr, size_t new_size)
This function tries to resize the buffer in-place. If successful, it returns true and no copying is needed. If unsuccessful, it returns false and we need to allocate another buffer, move our data there and release this buffer using free.
This function doesn’t exist; nevertheless, we will try to build it in this post!
Do you need to discuss a performance problem in your project? Or maybe you want a
vectorization training
for yourself or your team?
Contact us
Or follow us on
LinkedIn
,
Twitter
or
Mastodon
and get notified as soon as new content becomes available.
How to build
resize_buffer
?
If you are working with buffers that are smaller than memory page size (typical 4 kB), and you want to implement
resize_buffer
for all buffer sizes, this can come with a huge memory overhead. In essence, you will need to reserve a whole memory page (e.g. 4 kB) to allow your buffer to grow from 1 byte to 4 kB.
Growing larger buffers is easier. A common 64-bit system with virtual memory support (which is essentially all desktop and server CPUs and some more powerful embedded CPUs) have a memory address space that is 2^48 bits, or 256x4GB of data. If we want to allocate a growable buffer, we need to pick an address somewhere in this space at which we will allocate our buffer. Let’s say, we picked address X and the size of our buffer is 1 MB.
Let’s assume now that we want to grow our buffer from 1 MB to 4 MB. To achieve this, the following needs to be true:
The virtual memory from address X + 1MB to X + 3 MB needs to be unused – nobody else should have allocated this virtual memory space earlier.
The system should have additional 3 MB of physical memory to back up the virtual memory
Then, we can either ask the OS to expand the original virtual memory block from X + 1 MB to X + 3 MB. Alternatively, we can ask the OS to allocate a new memory block of 3 MB at address X + 1 MB.
Growing buffer on 32 bit system is the same, except that instead of 256×4 GB we have 4 GB of virtual memory space at our disposal. Growing memory is possible here as well, but  there is a much larger chance that the virtual address space we want to grow to is used by someone else.
On Linux
On Linux, memory is allocated using
mmap
system call. This call returns a block of memory which is a multiple of page size (the size in bytes, but the actually allocated memory will be rounded up to a multiple of page size, so e.g. 20 byte allocation will actually be a 4 kB allocation). Here is a an example on how to allocate memory using
mmap
:
void * res = mmap(base_addr, size, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0);
Important parameter is
base_addr
, which suggests to
mmap
the address we want to use – if
nullptr
, the OS will pick an address for us; otherwise the OS will try to allocate the specified address (if rounded to page size).
Unfortunately, in our testing environment, we couldn’t let Linux pick the base address for us: if we do this,  the next call to
mremap
will fail. The reason for the failure is that
mmap
tries to be conservative – and it reserves memory after your block so your block cannot grow.
Therefore, we have to provide a base address
43540070.article_summary:
本文讨论了在软件项目中避免数据拷贝以提升性能的方法，特别关注操作系统层面的支持。在C语言中，`realloc`函数可以在原地扩展或缩小内存，避免数据拷贝，但在C++中没有类似功能，只能使用`new`和`delete`。对于非平凡可复制类型，甚至不能使用`realloc`，需要手动构造和销毁对象。

为解决此问题，文章提出实现一个`resize_buffer`函数，尝试在原地调整缓冲区大小。对于小于内存页的缓冲区，这种方法可能导致巨大内存开销。而对于大缓冲区，可以通过操作系统的虚拟内存功能实现扩展。

在Linux上，使用`mmap`系统调用分配内存，并通过指定`base_addr`来确保缓冲区可扩展性。文章还提到在测试环境中，让系统自动选择地址会导致扩展失败，因此必须手动提供地址。

最后，文章邀请读者联系Johnny’s Software Lab LLC讨论性能问题或获取培训。

data.author: squircle
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了一个关于“地球空洞说”的奇特故事。1869年，美国医生西勒斯·里德·蒂德因电击事故后，自称是耶稣化身，并提出地球是一个内凹的球体，人类生活在内部。他创立了“科瑞什教”并试图证明这一理论。这一想法其实早在17世纪由著名科学家埃德蒙·哈雷提出，他认为地球内部有多层同心壳结构，解释地磁场变化。尽管该理论缺乏依据，但在当时基于有限的科学知识，哈雷的推论看似合理。类似观点也出现在世界各地的民间传说中，例如德国学者阿塔纳斯·基尔舍尔在1664年提出的地球内部有火和地下湖的观点。尽管这些理论在现代看来荒诞不经，但它们反映了早期科学与宗教交织时代的思维方式。

In 1869 an
American physician named Cyrus Reed Teed, whose very own brand of medicine combined alchemy with zaps of electricity and doses of magnetism, electrocuted himself so badly that he passed out. Which is just as well, for when he came to, he realized he was the living incarnation of Jesus Christ. Not only that, he also decided that the Earth is actually an inverted sphere: We line the inside and look
in on
, not
out to
, the rest of the universe.
So he started a cult called
Koreshanity
in Florida to convince the world of his geologic discovery. And on a beach near their commune, for five months the Koreshanites deployed the rectilliniator, a device of their own creation, to scientifically measure that the Earth is in fact concave. Naturally, it was a success.
Madness, to be sure, but also the product of an idea put forth 200 years previous by one of history’s greatest scientific minds:
Edmond Halley
. You see, Halley noticed that the Earth’s magnetic field is rather unpredictable, with its lines shifting from year to year. And Halley, after whom the
famous comet
is named, reckoned that the Earth’s hollowness is to blame—we’re standing on an outermost shell with three more concentric shells within. And it’s the poles of these inner shells that throw off our magnetic field. Oh, and according to Halley, there’s undoubtedly life flourishing deep down there.
Variations in Earth's magnetic field from 1590 to 1990.
GIF:
Wikimedia
This is the strange tale of the hollow Earth, a theory that even Halley himself realized was a tad unbelievable. “If I shall seem to advance anything that looks like Extravagant or Romantick,” he wrote in 1692, “the Reader is desired to suspend his censure, till he have considered the force and number of the many arguments which concurr [sic] to make good so new and so bold a Supposition.”
Halley was actually working off of his friend Isaac Newton’s recently published masterpiece
Principia
, “the work that forms the foundation for modern physical science,” according to Bucknell University’s Duane Griffin
in his essay
"What Curiosity in the Structure: The Hollow Earth in Science." “Insofar as the publication of the
Principia
marks the beginning of modern science,” adds Griffin, “Halley’s hollow Earth theory can thus be treated as the first prediction of the modern scientific era.”
OK, well, off to an interesting start. But the idea of a hollow Earth was hardly a new one, Griffin notes. It appears in folklore the world over, not to mention elsewhere in Europe in Halley’s time. A German named Athansius Kircher, for instance, published
Mundus Subterraneus
in 1664, in which he claimed the Earth contains a central fire (kinda true, really) and vast underground lakes and lava chambers. At the north pole is a gaping vortex that sucks water down to the central fire, where it’s heated and expelled out the south pole, much to the delight of the penguins there, I'd imagine.
Athansius Kircher's fanciful imagining of Earth's interior from his work
Mundus Subterraneus. In fairness, though, he'd never been to the center of the planet before, unlike Brendan Fraser in the 2008 film
Journey to the End of an Actor's Career Center of the Earth
.
Source:
Archive.org
Kircher hadn’t a lick of data to back up his claims, but Halley sure did. As strange as it seems, his theory was wrong but well-reasoned given the scope of human knowledge at the time, and it often incorporated ideas from
Principia
, according to Griffin. Halley argued that the variations in Earth’s magnetic field couldn’t be due to some sort of magnetic body wandering around in rock, what with the rather solid nature of rock, so there must be unseen circles spinning around beneath our feet.
“The Earth is represented by the outward Circle,” he wrote, “and the three inward Circles are made nearly proportionable to the Magnitudes of the Planets Venus, Mars, and Mercury, all which may be included within this Globe of Earth.” There’s no danger of them ramming into each other, by the way, because like with Saturn’s concentric rings, they’re held in place perfectly well by gravity.
Edmond Halley, brilliant scientist and hater of smiles. Image:
Wikimedia
Because magnetism is a stronger force than gravity, the inside of the shell must be lined with “Magnetical Matter” that keeps the thing from crumbling and caving in on itself. There is the problem, though, of cracks forming in the outer shell, with gravity sucking ocean water and debris toward the center of the Earth. But Halley reckons that “Internal parts of this Bubble of Earth should be replete with such Saline and Vitrolick Particles” that would plug up a leak (he would later on in 1716 attribute a particularly intense bout of aurora borealis to luminous vapors escaping from a crack in the Earth).

主要讨论点：针对一种基于绩效的销售服务商业模式的可行性及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• [FloorEgg] 认为大多数初创公司缺乏产品与市场的契合度，许多产品无人想要。即使销售技巧再好，如果没有市场契合，结果也会很差。此外，风投公司也在努力寻找有市场需求的产品，但大多不成功。因此，FloorEgg认为销售技巧的作用被高估，市场契合度才是关键。
  
• [abxyz] 提到行业中有许多"成交高手"（closers），但他们的激励机制与企业不一致，往往会为了达成自己的目标而向不良客户销售产品。虽然这种模式有可能成功，但市场中存在大量劣质服务，导致企业对此模式持谨慎态度。

• [cj] 认为这种模式类似于“联盟营销”模式，在小型公司中可能更有吸引力。然而，随着公司发展壮大，企业更倾向于支付固定费用而非依赖绩效支付模式，因为后者可能难以实现关键收入目标。

• [edoceo] 表示其初创公司每周收到多次类似推销，但这些推销与公司业务线无关。作为投资者，他认为创始人应亲自进行早期销售，且不认为资本难以筹集。

• [bradley13] 分享了自己的经历，表明他曾因讨厌销售而考虑过类似服务，但由于找不到愿意基于绩效支付的营销机构，最终没有采用这种模式。

• [soared] 认为这种模式下，销售人员的学习成本高且成效不确定，对于公司来说可能不划算。

• [rwallace] 认为这种模式有趣且降低了尝试的风险，尽管存在一些问题，但值得探讨。

• [nickdothutton] 提到这种模式在1990年代的英国曾非常成功，尤其是在美国科技公司进入欧洲市场时，但这些销售人员通常后来被客户公司聘用。

• [pickle-wizard] 分享了在一家初创公司中使用销售代理但未成功的经验，表明代理不理解产品且缺乏动力，因此认为合同中应包含退出条款。

• [jocaal] 认为商业模式的成功与否无法预知，很多看似不合理的模式也可能带来成功。如果决定尝试这种模式，需要承担一定风险。

• [notahacker] 指出需要考虑这种模式对服务提供者的吸引力，特别是在面对产品市场契合度有限的企业时，存在选择偏差问题，即最有可能接受这种模式的公司往往是市场准备不足的公司。

• [brudgers] 认为外包销售意味着不直接与潜在客户交流，这种模式虽然心理上更具吸引力，但外包销售人员的激励机制与公司不一致，可能导致问题。

data.title: Cyber Forensic Expert in 2k Cases Faces FBI Probe
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 明尼苏达州的网络安全和计算机取证专家马克·兰特曼（Mark Lanterman）正面临对其资历的质疑及联邦调查局（FBI）的调查。兰特曼曾在数千起案件中提供专家证词，但被指控虚报拥有Upsala College的学士和硕士学位，以及在哈佛大学的网络安全研究生学习经历。经调查，这些声称无法被证实。他的LinkedIn资料和公司网站信息已被删除，亨内平县检察官办公室通知了十个未决案件的相关方。 Perkins Coie律师事务所要求法院排除兰特曼的证词，称其背景不实，甚至带走其曾在宾夕法尼亚州Springfield Township警察局的个人档案以掩盖经历。此事可能导致许多已判决案件重新审理。
